claim: Exact nesting of five separate per-level DCELs is unrealisable on the integer lattice
claim_full: The hard invariant 'every L(n+1) face inside one L(n) face' cannot hold with five separate per-level DCELs on a 1 cm lattice: any child vertex computed on an inherited parent edge (plot side line on a kerb, wedge boundary on a spine, footprint corner on a plot line, bridge spine across an inherited shoreline, stage-2 plot on a shared kerb) snaps off that edge, so the child protrudes or leaves a gap that exact predicates detect on nearly every batch; §13.1's 'children areas sum to the parent within 1 cm²' fails too, and §2.3's level-set faces break single-parent L0 nesting.
required_change: Add a cross-level vertex protocol: a splitThrough(edge, latticePoint) op that inserts the vertex into every level carrying the inherited edge in the same batch (or one shared vertex/edge store with level-tagged edges and per-level face records); state nesting topologically (child boundary edges coincide with parent edges by vertex ids or lie strictly inside) and check it exactly; replace the §13.1 area test with exact integer tiling; make level sets L0 'contour' edges, never faces; amend J-6/D-13 and the 'L3 never touches L1 memory' rule.
evidence: ARCH §2.2, §3.2 (1), §5.3 (hard, abort, 0/1 000), J-6, D-13, §13.1, II.1/II.5. Executed (scratchpad nesting_check.out): 61 % of random 5–60 m edges have no interior lattice point; 99.8 % of snapped feet lie strictly off the parent edge (max 0.70 cm); re-routing triangle > 1 cm² in 99.6 %. os-geometry.md §1.1: the 2017 shared-Point topology moved shared boundaries atomically; PLAT keeps that only within a level.

claim: A wall-clock watchdog changes the model, so the same seed gives different towns on different machines
claim_full: F-BUDGET-TIME switches a stage to 'coarser parameters' when a wall-clock watchdog fires, the kernel returns E_TIMEOUT, and F-SKELETON detects failure by timeout; the same seed therefore yields different towns on slow, throttled or loaded machines, breaking identical hashes, K-3 snapshot verification, permalinks, edit replay and goldens.
required_change: Make every output-affecting budget a deterministic work budget (kernel calls, proposals, candidates, skeleton events, depth) and rename E_TIMEOUT to an operation-count E_WORK_LIMIT; restrict F-BUDGET-TIME to reporting and to deferring when a lazy tier runs, never what it computes (a deferred tier must hash identically); keep the watchdog outside model packages (cancel-and-resume only); add a CI golden run under a 10× time-dilation shim that must be byte-identical.
evidence: ARCH §5.2 (F-BUDGET-TIME, F-SKELETON rows), §3.1 KernelError E_TIMEOUT, §14 Stage.budgetMs, §12 (252 ms p50 vs 300 ms p95, 'thin'); contradicts §6.5 (3) (no Date/performance.now in model packages), §6.5 (5) (no stage reads timing), §6.2 (model is a pure function), O2 (a)/O3 (e), and the one-page goal 'same seed … same town on every machine'.

claim: The 5 cm weld / 25 cm minEdge dead band rejects about one cut in ten, and F-NUM cannot repair it
claim_full: insertChain welds within 5 cm but rejects features below 25 cm, so any crossing/endpoint 5–25 cm from an existing vertex is neither welded nor legal; on Chaikin-smoothed spines ≈10 % of two-ended cuts and plot lines hit this band, so nearly every S8/S10 batch uses the ladder (§13.5 '≤ 2 % of transactions' unattainable), F-NUM's 1 cm perturbation / 10 cm simplification cannot move a vertex 20 cm, and its last rung 'reject the chain' drops mandatory chains (wall, coast, bank, arterial, user way, plot line).
required_change: Add vertex attraction: new vertices within minEdge of an existing vertex snap to it (nearest, id tie-break); endpoints within minEdge of an edge snap onto it (splitThrough); weld only hot-pixel coincidences; split F-NUM by chain class — optional chains may be rejected, mandatory chains get an always-succeeding rung (re-insert with attraction, then minEdge simplification with topology checks); re-state the ladder-use metric.
evidence: ARCH §2.2 lattice + rule 2, §3.1, §4.3, §5.2 F-NUM, §13.5. Executed deadband_check.out: Chaikin×2 of 25–40 m steps → segments p50 7.9 m; P(endpoint in band) 0.052, per cut 0.101. FTG fixed editing errors with 'improved intersection snapping' (157283634); MFCG 2017 merged junctions < 8 units (_critic-os row 37).

claim: One type and one entity per half-edge cannot represent coincident features; sliver absorption deletes typed edges
claim_full: Each half-edge holds one type (an enum of 22 values) and one entity, yet coincident roles are built in: district boundaries are 'always spine edges', quays run on shores, walls are pulled/snapped to river banks, fields end on tracks; insertChain's collinear-overlap behaviour is unspecified (one role overwrites the other), and sliver absorption 'into the neighbour with the longer shared boundary' deletes a way/wall/shore edge, leaving gaps in streets or walls.
required_change: Store a role set per edge ((role, entity) pairs in a side table); insertChain merges roles on collinear overlap, never duplicates or overwrites; slivers are resolved by collapsing the two near-parallel chains into one chain carrying both role sets, never by deleting an edge whose roles include way/wall/shore/bank; add coincident-feature fixtures.
evidence: ARCH §2.2 (halfEdges.type Uint16Array, entity Int32Array; rule 1), §2.4 type list, §3.1 sliver merge, §4.8 (trace to banks, quays), §5.2 F-WALL 'snap to the water outline', F-CORRIDOR. FTG F9 (_critic-ftg): 120 water-outline edges double as lot edges — coincident roles are normal.

claim: Raw arena indices are persisted in entity records, seam contracts and edit events, with no lineage on split, merge or weld
claim_full: Entities, seam contracts and edit events persist raw arena indices (HalfEdgeId in Way.spine, Enceinte.trace, Plot.frontage/access/partyWalls, Frontage.edge, Building.entrance.edge, SeamEdge.edge; VertexId in Junction/Tower and moveVertex; FaceId in regenerate scopes) while only face ids are promised stable; every split/merge/weld renumbers them, so Way.spine goes stale during S8 generation itself and logged VertexIds/FaceIds hit unrelated geometry after an upgrade replay.
required_change: Make geometry references kernel-maintained handles: a per-batch lineage table (split/merge/weld emit old→new mappings; stored chains are rewritten before commit; an invariant checks every handle resolves) or chains stored as role tags walked on demand; edit events and API scopes address geometry by stable entity id + quantised world position, never VertexId/FaceId; B-EDIT asserts 0 stale handles.
evidence: ARCH §2.4–§2.7 interfaces, II.1 SeamContract/SeamReport, §7.1 EditEvent, §14 Scope, §2.2 rule 2 (face-id stability only). FTG 153121107 (ftg-posts-c §2.14): after edits, stale graph state (two intersections at one position) broke district re-roll.

claim: `splitFace` does not define contact for the degenerate cases the lattice makes common
claim_full: splitFace's 'exactly two boundary crossings' is undefined for the degeneracies the lattice makes routine — endpoint on an edge interior, cut through a vertex, grazing a reflex vertex, collinear overlap, antennae (cul-de-sacs, drainage lines), and outer-ring-to-hole 'slits' that join cycles instead of splitting — so valid cuts are rejected or pinched/non-manifold faces are committed; faces keeping antennae also export as self-touching GeoJSON rings (O11 d).
required_change: Specify contact semantics: the cut touches the boundary only at its two endpoints; endpoints are a boundary vertex or an on-edge point inserted by splitThrough; interior contact (vertex graze, overlap) is E_NOT_TWO_CROSSINGS; antenna edges count as boundary for endpoints (a declared T-junction); the GeoJSON exporter drops antennae from face rings; hole-joining cuts are a separate connectHole op with its own post-conditions; add a constructive fixture per case.
evidence: ARCH §3.4 splitFace, §4.6 step 5 and 'Holes' (a slit has one child), §4.4 (dead ends kept deliberately), §2.3 drainage lines as L0 edges. 2017 cut() silently returned its input on ≠ 2 crossings incl. > 2 on concave shapes (os-geometry §2.1.5); its buffer ignored crossings near endpoints (§2.1.4 (c)).

claim: The null-OBB class survives: the OBB contract contradicts itself, and NaN or ±∞ silently become vertices at the origin
claim_full: The OBB row contradicts itself ('< 3 non-collinear points → Degenerate' vs 'collinear hull → OBB with zero minor extent, reported'); consumers divide by the minor extent, the resulting NaN/±∞ is stored by Int32Array as 0, so a vertex silently jumps to the world origin; the only guard is a debug-build isInteger assert, and a two-comparison range check passes NaN — MFCG's null 'rect' crash class survives as silent corruption.
required_change: One OBB contract (collinear or < 3 distinct points → Degenerate, never ok-with-zero-extent); all ratios through a checked-division helper returning typed results; the snap function rejects non-finite/out-of-range input in all builds with !(Math.abs(x) < 2**23) → E_OUT_OF_RANGE; fixtures for collinear hulls and zero-area residues.
evidence: ARCH §3.1 OBB row and E_OUT_OF_RANGE, §2.2 'asserted Number.isInteger in debug builds', §3.2 (1). Executed (Node): Int32Array [NaN, Infinity, 2^31+5] → [0, 0, −2147483643]; (x ≥ L || x ≤ −L) does not flag NaN. MFCG 61026228 'the variable rect ends up null' (mfcg-posts-b §2.3); 2017 MathUtils.sign(NaN) = +1 (_critic-os row 132).

claim: The straight skeleton's "exact rational event times" are impossible; near-simultaneous events are the normal case for roofs, and nothing validates the output
claim_full: The skeleton's 'event queue on exact rational times' is impossible (unit-speed offsets make event times involve √(dx²+dy²) of lattice edges); near-simultaneous events are the norm for roofs (rectangles, squares), 67 % of snapped rotated squares lose their single apex to a micro-ridge whose orientation flips under 1 cm changes, and no output validator is specified — F-SKELETON detects only 'inconsistency, timeout', so crossing-arc glitches reach roofs, label spines and glTF.
required_change: Specify doubles with + − × ÷ √ only, a world-length event-coalescing tolerance and id tie-breaks; build near-rectangular footprints' roofs from the OBB (exact apex/ridge) and keep the skeleton for irregular outlines and spines; add a post-condition validator (planar skeleton, monotone faces, consistent heights) whose failure triggers the typed downgrade under a work-count (not time) limit; add rotated-rectangle/square/n-gon fixtures.
evidence: ARCH §3.1 skeleton row, §4.7 S11 hip roofs, §9 spines, §11 glTF, §5.2 F-SKELETON. _critic.md spot-check 20 (101173551: own O(n²) skeleton, 'glitches in special cases'). Executed pitot_check.out: tangential 33.4 %, |a+c−b−d| p90 1.4 cm (a convex quad has one skeleton node iff tangential).

claim: Two boolean engines with different numerics ship, and the fallback cannot offset
claim_full: Two boolean engines with different numerics ship (Clipper2 WASM plus a pure-JS polygon-clipping 'fallback'; §13.1 accepts equality 'within one lattice unit'), so any host running the fallback (no WASM, CSP without 'wasm-unsafe-eval', instantiation failure) produces a different model hash for the same seed; the fallback has no offsetting, so corridorUnion/offsetFace/insetRing/bufferChain have no implementation on that path. The deferred choice covers which library wins M0, not a second runtime engine.
required_change: One geometry engine per generator version on every host (Clipper2 WASM or a pure-TS port everywhere, hard reported failure instead of a fallback — or the TS port as the only engine); polygon-clipping only as a CI oracle; an engine change is a version bump with a declared golden shift; record in D-14.
evidence: ARCH §1.7, §3.1 booleans/offset rows, §13.1, §14 adapter 'Clipper2 WASM | polygon-clipping', §17 'fallback polygon-clipping', D-14 'with a pure-JS fallback', deferrals list. polygon-clipping exposes union/intersection/xor/difference only (library API; confirm in M0). FTG uses a WASM Clipper (js-angusj-clipper, ftg-posts-b T-17).

claim: The vertex-move predicate for smoothing and warp is wrong, and warp has no level across five separate DCELs
claim_full: Smoothing and warp validate moves per vertex ('never moves a vertex across another edge; the step is halved'), which misses incident edges sweeping over other vertices and simultaneous brush moves where two vertices pass each other; the warp event has no level, so across five separate DCELs a shared boundary moves by different amounts per level (nesting breaks) or only L1 moves and everything under the brush is re-rolled on each stroke.
required_change: Validate a whole step: apply all moves on the overlay, test edges incident to moved vertices (incl. other moved edges) and unmoved vertices against swept triangles; on failure halve the whole step's strength deterministically; define warp as a displacement field on a declared level set (L0–L1) with finer levels transported via GEO-1's shared-vertex protocol and re-derived only where invariants fail (logged); add the level to the event.
evidence: ARCH §3.1 curves row, §3.4 warp, §7.1 warp event (no level field), §7.4 moveVertex/warp row; MFCG warp semantics (_critic.md C4/C5); os-geometry §1.1 (shared Points moved every polygon atomically — the property MFCG's warp relied on).

claim: Weld makes the plat depend on insertion order, so the locality oracle and the K-3 load check cannot pass for geometric edits
claim_full: Weld-to-nearest-existing-vertex and the minEdge rejection make the plat depend on insertion order; drawn ways enter interactively after generation but 'before the stage that would create the class' on replay, so the §7.3 locality oracle ('incremental hash equals from-scratch hash', an M3 exit criterion) fails or becomes vacuous, and K-3 reports spurious snapshot/replay mismatches on every edited document.
required_change: Canonicalise insertion within a batch (sort candidate chains by stable key; lattice snap rounding for topology; attraction per GEO-3 in canonical order); make the interactive path for drawn constraints identical to the replay path (re-run from the constraint's stage for the affected scope, same batch order); restate the oracle as 'log-order replay equals session state' plus a separate outside-scope byte-identity test.
evidence: ARCH §2.2 rule 2, §3.1 lattice row, §7.2 (constraints inserted before the stage), §7.3 oracle, §2.9 K-3 policy, §13.2, §16 M3 exit. Hot-pixel snap rounding is order-independent; weld-to-existing is not.

claim: B-FUZZ's random inputs almost never hit exact degeneracies, and two of its stated properties are wrong
claim_full: B-FUZZ's 10⁶ random polygons almost never produce exact degeneracies (points exactly on segments, collinear triples, cuts through vertices, overlaps, simultaneous skeleton events, quantisation-boundary values: ≤ 2^-24 per random triple), so O3 (a) can pass with every degenerate class untested; §13.1 also states two wrong properties ('splitFace children areas sum to the parent within 1 cm²'; 'the straight skeleton a tree … hole-aware').
required_change: Add constructive degeneracy generators (gcd-stepped on-segment points, overlaps, vertex-through and reflex-graze cuts, antennae, coincident typed chains, snapped rotated rectangles/squares/n-gons, holes touching the outer ring, quantisation-boundary values) held to the same 0-crash/0-invalid bar; correct the two properties (exact integer tiling; skeleton connected with cycle count = hole count).
evidence: ARCH §13.1, §5.2 F-NUM test column, §15.2 O3 (a). Arithmetic: a line across a 2^24 frame holds at most 2^24 of its 2^48 lattice points. Executed nesting_check.out (area property fails 99.6 %); a skeleton of a polygon with h holes has h independent cycles.

claim: S1's closed-outline routine has no simplicity guarantee (islands, fjords, sky islands)
claim_full: The S1 closed-outline routine (coast, lakes, ponds, islands, sky islands) displaces a base curve by domain-warped fBm with no bound relative to the curve's local feature size, so small islands, elongated sky-island ovals (end radius of curvature ≈ b²/a) and fjord intents self-intersect; insertChain then splits them into extra loops whose land/water type is undefined, or F-NUM drops the coast.
required_change: Bound normal displacement to ≈ 0.8 × the local feature size (distance to the base curve's medial axis on that side), or repair with a non-zero union that keeps the anchor's component and types the rest by rule, with a report; property test 10 000 outlines per intent → 0 self-intersections, 0 untyped loops.
evidence: ARCH §4.2 S1 (2) (one routine; amplitude envelope damps detail only near the town), §3.1 (self-touching chains split into simple runs), §2.1/§2.7 SkyIsland. FTG 153121107: a self-intersecting ocean shape 'broke some of the logic in the server' (ftg-posts-c §2.12); VG discards maps whose highway 'intersects itself' (_critic-vg-ng P1).

claim: "Contours and coast agree by construction" is false, and the hard invariant that polices it has no ladder
claim_full: 'Contours and coast agree by construction' is false: a 5–10 m raster lowered below sea level on the sea side of a cm-precision vector coast yields marching-squares contours that cross the vector coast at diagonal cell crossings, around sub-cell spits and inlets, and repeatedly on cliff/steep coasts; 'contours never cross a shore' is a hard invariant with no ladder, so S1 aborts and a steep-coast town is never produced.
required_change: Either extract the shoreline as the sea-level set of the same field (VG's construction; smooth only within a cell), or keep the vector coast, give coastal land cells a monotone ramp ≥ sea level + ε and clip every contour to the land faces in vector space before emission; replace the abort with that construction plus a clip rung; add steep-coast fixtures.
evidence: ARCH §2.3 (raster 5/8/10 m), §4.2 S1 (2) 'lowered below sea level on the sea side, so contours and coast agree by construction', S1 (7) cliff banks, §5.3 hard invariant, §5.2 (no F-row), O1 (b)/R11. VG achieves agreement because its water outline is a level set of the carved field (_critic-vg-ng V2, V8).

claim: Terrain heights in `Int16Array` centimetres overflow at 327.67 m, and flats after priority-flood are unresolved
claim_full: Terrain heightCm is an Int16Array (−327.68…+327.67 m 'above datum'); typed-array stores wrap silently, so hilly/mountainous relief, hill-acropolis sites or a sea-level datum with hills over 327 m turn summits into deep pits that priority-flood fills into mountain-top lakes and D8 routes rivers through; the flats priority-flood creates also leave D8 directions undefined without a stated flat-resolution rule.
required_change: Store heights as Int32 cm (or Int16 dm with a declared ±3.2 km range) relative to a per-document datum, with a range check that reports instead of wrapping; specify flat resolution after priority-flood (ε-gradient toward the spill point or Garbrecht–Martz); add mountainous-relief fixtures.
evidence: ARCH §2.3 (heightCm: Int16Array; D8 with sinks filled), §4.2 S1 (1) relief characters 'flat / rolling / hilly / mountainous' and site primitives, S1 (3), §7.7 forms (hill-acropolis). Executed (Node): Int16Array[40000] → −25536. FTG's 'Mountains aren't properly supported yet' is the weakness O1 answers (_critic-ftg §2).

claim: S4 smooths each route separately, so shared runs become braided near-duplicate spines
claim_full: S4 routes each destination pair separately and simplifies/smooths each path before inserting it, so routes that share lattice edges leaving the plaza become braided near-parallel spines (welded where < 5 cm, crossing each other, dead-band rejections, slivers absorbed with an edge deleted) — the duplicate-intersection class; the 8 m junction merge moves vertices and is validated only at the single S4 batch commit.
required_change: Build the arterial graph first (union of lattice edges used by all routes with multiplicity, split at degree ≠ 2, 8 m merge on the graph), then simplify/smooth once per graph chain between pinned junctions, set class/width from multiplicity or betweenness, and insert each chain once; test that no two spines run closer than the class separation for more than one step length.
evidence: ARCH §4.3 (per-route Visvalingam + Chaikin×2 + curvature limit, 'junctions welded', merge < 8 m), §4.1 (S4 one batch). MFCG 2017 needed tidyUpRoads to de-duplicate central runs shared by streets to different gates (_critic-os C6, S8); FTG 153121107 'two different intersections could have the same world position … this breaks things'.

claim: Bridges must be within ±10° of the channel normal (a hard invariant), but nothing constructs that angle
claim_full: 'Bridges within ± 10° of the channel normal' is a hard invariant, but S4 crosses rivers along jittered-hex lattice edges and then smooths the path, so the crossing angle follows the destinations, not the river; §4.8 describes a perpendicular deck but not how the way reaches it. Read on the way, the invariant fails on most crossings with no F-row (river towns abort); read on the deck, it holds while the spine crosses the water at another angle, so road and deck disagree.
required_change: Make S1 (5) emit each crossing site as a pinned bank-to-bank deck perpendicular to local flow; S4 routes to the deck endpoints as a fixed graph edge, with approach curves within the class radius; smoothing never moves deck vertices; add an F-ROUTE rung that moves the site along its reach when the approaches cannot meet the radius.
evidence: ARCH §4.3 (lattice, A*, Chaikin×2), §4.2 S1 (5) crossing sites, §4.8 water furniture, §5.3 hard invariant, §5.2 (no ladder). VG makes bridge angles 'as right as possible' (89314043; _critic-vg-ng S8).

claim: The wall trace is drawn after streets and districts and pulled up to 40 m: ungated secondary crossings have no remedy
claim_full: The enceinte is traced after S5 grows the stage's secondaries and S6 types its districts, then pulled up to 40 m to defensible ground; inward pulls cross non-arterial streets, violating the hard 'walls not crossed except at gates' invariant, and F-WALL's only clearing rung (larger radius) discards the defensible pull; districts typed before the wall straddle it, and the trace's Visvalingam step is not topology-preserving. MFCG avoided this by building walls before streets.
required_change: Compute the pulled/smoothed/simplified trace in S5's boundary step before growth and grow inside it, reserving gates where arterials cross; S5 legality forbids non-gate crossings (stop at the setback band or become a postern by rule); S6 treats the trace as a barrier; make trace simplification topology-preserving; add a last reported F-WALL rung that cuts the way at the setback band and prunes short outer stubs.
evidence: ARCH §4.1 (S7 after S6 types the stage's districts), §4.4 (boundary = wall candidate), §4.5 validateEdge, §4.8 (40 m pull; Visvalingam 20 m / angle ≥ 100°), §5.2 F-WALL, §5.3. MFCG 2017 walls precede streets and block wall vertices except gates (_critic-os row 61, §4.2); FTG's 6 and 2 ungated crossings (ARCH §13.5) are the weakness O8 targets.

claim: Harbour basins, moats and canals are carved into L0 after the streets and districts already cover that ground
claim_full: Harbour basins ('carved from the waterfront district'), moats and canals ('along a chosen way') are inserted into L0 in S7, after S4/S5 spines and S6 districts already occupy that ground: spines end up in water, typed district faces are cut, quays land on the new shore with half a corridor over water, and no rule says which spines are cut, rerouted or deleted — contrary to the design's own 'water before roads' order.
required_change: Reserve basin, moat and canal footprints at S3 as siting claims sized from port demand and carve them into L0 before S4, so routing, growth and typing see water; generate quays/piers on the reserved shore; route any later carve (an edit) through the conversion path with explicit cut/reroute rules and lifecycle events.
evidence: ARCH §4.8 water furniture (basin, moles, quays, piers, moat, canals), §4.1 (S7 after S6), §4 plain-words order rationale, §4.2 S3 (harbour candidate). FTG creates harbours as part of waterfront districts before plots/buildings (130937474; _critic-ftg F11 and §2).

claim: The kerb is built three different ways, and per-edge insets of concave faces have no primitive
claim_full: The kerb is constructed three ways — S8's insetRing (per-edge distances only on the convex half-plane path, a uniform Clipper offset for concave faces) and S9's buffer-union-subtract with round joins — so concave mixed-class faces (the organic norm) have no correct inset, near-collinear class changes are mis-inset (a 2° kink with 3 m Δhalf-width lets the wider offset govern ≈ 86 m), and blocks/cut feet sized on S8's kerb disagree with S9's committed blocks.
required_change: Define the kerb once as a kernel function: kerb(L1 face) = face − ⋃ buffer(spine_i, halfwidth_i) with declared joins; S8 partitions the L2 blocks it yields (materialise S9 for the district's coarse spines first, update L2 locally after each cut); keep the half-plane path only for uniform convex insets; test S8 working polygon ≡ S9 committed block (Hausdorff 0).
evidence: ARCH §3.1 offsetting row, §3.4 offsetFace/insetRing/corridorUnion, §4.6 ('after insetRing by the corridor half-widths'), §4.7 S9. The 2017 author: shrink 'Works very well for convex polygons, not so much concave ones'; buffer is reliable 'only if all distances are equal. Otherwise weird steps are created' (os-geometry §2.1.4 (b), (c)). NG subtracts the corridor within the cut (_critic-vg-ng V19).

claim: S8 turns NG's drawing rule into model topology: cut spines end at the kerb, not at the crossed spine
claim_full: §4.6 imports NG's drawing rule ('ends stop at the crossed corridor's edge') into the model: cuts are computed on the inset polygon and end on kerbs, yet are inserted as L1 lane spines, so they dangle as antennae — the L1 face is not split, there are no children to recurse on, the lane is not connected to the street graph (junction census, betweenness, R3 miss it), and S9's end-cap pokes into the crossed street.
required_change: In the model, extend each cut end along its arrival direction from the kerb to the crossed spine and insert a T-junction (splitThrough) so the L1 face splits and the lane joins the graph; keep 'stop at the corridor edge' as the renderer's stroke rule (square caps), which S9's corridor union and junction wedge already produce.
evidence: ARCH §4.6 step 7 and 'Cuts are inserted as lane / alley spines, so lanes are real ways in the same graph'. profile-neighbourhood BG-2 item 5 and BG-4 item 9 ('Draw. Stop each end exactly half the crossed road's width from its centreline' — a drawing rule); PF-1 step 1 had to extend every junction end to the crossed centreline to rebuild NG's planar graph.

claim: The bent cut's rules are undefined on curved, round-joined kerbs and on non-quadrilateral faces
claim_full: The bent cut's rules ('two OBB-major-parallel boundary runs', 'perpendicular to the start/far edge', 'within 2.5°') were measured on NG faces whose sides are straight runs, but the fusion applies them inside Chaikin×2-smoothed, curvature-continuous, round-joined kerbs where every 'side' is a single 1–9 m segment: perpendiculars follow segment noise, the straight/bent test flips randomly, and triangles, C-shapes and holed faces have no two major-parallel runs.
required_change: Define sides as maximal runs within a turning tolerance (e.g. 10° cumulative) with chord directions; measure perpendicularity against run chords or a ±5 m tangent window, not the hit segment; define start/far sides for non-quadrilateral faces (e.g. the two runs with greatest projection on the OBB major axis; far side per AN-6's perpendicular ray); add curved and round-joined faces to M0 fixtures and re-measure the NG signature on them before calibration.
evidence: ARCH §4.6 steps 1–3, §4.3 (Chaikin×2, curvature limit), §4.4 (curvature-continuous headings). profile-neighbourhood PF-1 step 4 (sides broken at every ≥ 1° turn; fillets replaced by virtual corners), PF-3 (ring faces looser), AN-2 (ring σ 0.098 vs 0.066 plain), AN-3 (perpendicular ray names the far side in 66 %); deadband_check.out (segments p50 7.9 m).

claim: The F-CUT ladder turns large concave faces into single court blocks — MFCG's "empty areas inside walls" returns
claim_full: F-CUT's rungs (b) mean-normal cut and (c) OBB-centre axis cut assume near-convex faces (for L/C shapes or faces holding a cul-de-sac the OBB centre can lie outside and the axis line crosses four times), so they fail together and rung (d) turns the whole face — possibly 0.5–1 ha — into one block with a court; S10 then leaves a ~40 × 40 m unbuilt interior: MFCG's 'empty areas … inside city walls' glitch, which §3.5 does not list.
required_change: Add FTG's reflex pre-cut (and splits at antenna roots) before the bent cut; add an always-succeeding rung before (d): a straight cut perpendicular to the longest side run through its midpoint, clipped to the face's component by boolean intersection; allow rung (d) only for faces ≤ 2 × the band's upper block area; report per district the built-area share left as court/green residue, bounded (e.g. ≤ 5 %).
evidence: ARCH §4.6 step 5, §5.2 F-CUT, §5.1 tier 5, §3.5, §4.4 (dead ends kept). MFCG 87882877 'Empty areas where they clearly shouldn't be, e.g. inside city walls'; 98918904 glitch 'remains … hard to fix' (mfcg-posts-b §2.3). FTG 133016301: old cut 'struggles … with internal corners', fixed by 'first cut perpendicular to interior corners' (ftg-posts-c §2.1).

claim: Frontage-first strips overlap or cross at reflex corners and concave frontages; "never emits hourglasses" is only asserted
claim_full: S10 lays strips perpendicular to each frontage with a corner rule for convex corners only; at reflex corners (notches around cul-de-sac corridors, blocks wrapped round claimed sub-faces, the inside of curves tighter than the plot depth) strips overlap or side lines cross before depth, giving overlapping or hourglass plots; §3.5's 'frontage-first construction never emits them' is asserted, and the hard invariants then rely on F-PLOT fallbacks, eroding 'discard 0 by construction'.
required_change: Partition each block into per-frontage regions before laying strips — via the block's straight skeleton (one region per frontage edge, depth capped by skeleton height) or FTG's reflex pre-cut — then lay strips inside regions and type seam wedges as residue or corner plots; property test on concave, notched and curved blocks: 0 overlapping or self-intersecting plots before any fallback.
evidence: ARCH §4.7 S10 (4)–(6), §3.5 hourglass row, §5.2 F-PLOT, §15.2 O5 (b), (f). FTG 133016301: L-shapes, arrowheads, hourglasses 'come from buildings wrapping around interior corners', and the filters 'do not detect everything (e.g. hourglass shaped buildings)' (ftg-posts-c §2.1); NG discards 42 % of lot leaves (_critic-vg-ng V18).

claim: S10's rear lanes write L1 from a per-block L3 batch, leaving sibling blocks stale in an unbounded loop
claim_full: S10 (one L3 batch per block) inserts rear lanes 'as a lane spine (back to the L1 graph, then S9 re-materialises locally)', writing L1 from an L3 batch against 'L(n+1) = refine_n(L(n))' and 'a transaction on L3 never touches L1 memory'; sibling blocks of the same L1 face keep already-committed plots that now overlap the new corridor, and the S10 → L1 → S9 → S10 loop has no stated bound.
required_change: Decide rear and back lanes in S8, where districts are already typed and the depth bands are known, so S10 never writes L1; if S10 must add a lane, model it as a deferred L1 edit that re-runs S9 and S10 for the whole affected L1 face in one transaction, with a declared iteration bound.
evidence: ARCH §2.2 rules 1 and 4, §4.7 S10 (8), §4.1 (S10 one batch per block), §3.3 KernelTx (one level per transaction), §5.3 (nesting; 'no way centreline crosses a footprint').

claim: Row-house footprints fitted as frontage-aligned rectangles cannot share bent or curved party walls
claim_full: Row houses are built as 'an inset rectangle or L aligned to the frontage', but S10's side lines are bent and frontages curve, so neighbouring rectangles cannot share the party-wall edge — they gap or overlap; the hard 'no footprint overlap' invariant then drives F-SITEPLAN's downgrades (coverage → compound → detached → hovel → vacant) and the attached share the design promises collapses.
required_change: Build row footprints by clipping, not fitting: footprint = plot ∩ frontage band of the row depth (boolean intersection with the plot), so the party wall is the plot side line by construction; build L4 per block in one batch so a party wall is one shared edge; keep rectangles for detached and compound slots; property test attached and party-wall shares on curved-street blocks.
evidence: ARCH §4.7 S10 (4) (bent side lines), S11 row arrangement, §2.6 OutlineBuildingGenerator, §5.2 F-SITEPLAN, §5.3, §13.5 (NG 95–99 % attached, party walls 39–43 %; target attached ≥ 90 % dense/poor), §15.2 O17 (c).

claim: The one incremental path the base builds grows streets through built plots; nothing stops or converts them
claim_full: The one incremental path the base builds (M4: add a growth stage) runs S5 on the persisted L1 with legality rules that ignore faces already carrying L2–L4 content; new secondaries cross the previous ring's ribbon and suburb plots, so either corridors overlap existing footprints (batch aborts) or S8–S13 re-derive the touched faces and re-roll surviving buildings — against the owner's 'nothing that survives an epoch is re-rolled' and M4's '0 re-rolled survivors'.
required_change: Give incremental S5 a built-face legality class: proposals may not cross faces holding footprints unless a declared conversion applies (routes along plot boundaries/back lanes, or demolish events with lifecycle records and a cost); apply existingFabricCost to S5; re-cut plots cut by a new corridor through the conversion path (keep buildings that fit, demolish others with events), never re-derive from scratch; epoch test on a town with ribbon and suburb regimes.
evidence: ARCH §4.11 (grow: S5 on persisted L1; S8–S13 on new or changed faces), §4.4 (ribbon plots on the arterial; suburb small lots from the outset; legality list), §4.3 (existingFabricCost for S4 only), §16 M4 exit, D-25; owner EVOLUTION ruling.

claim: Per-district raster tiles break the global "every casing before any body" order at district seams, and adjacent fills leave seams
claim_full: Canvas2D keeps retained tiles per district (Mark.group = district at city LOD), but district boundaries are streets, so if way marks live in district tiles, the tile drawn later strokes the boundary street's casing across the mouth of every street meeting it from the other district (an ink bar at each boundary T-junction), breaking the global 'every casing before any body' law; adjacent partition fills also show anti-aliasing seams.
required_change: Cache only area/building marks per district; draw ribbon and linework marks (ways, rivers, walls, towers, piers) in per-band global passes (all casings, then all bodies) over the tiles — or tile a regular screen grid rendering every intersecting mark in global program order; draw same-semantic adjacent fills as unions or with NG's ½-px dilation; render test: no casing pixels inside junction mouths on district boundaries.
evidence: ARCH §8.1 Mark.group, §8.2 casing law, §8.5 tiles per district, §2.2 rule 1. visual-spec §1.3 items 3–7, 10–11 (MFCG: global casing then body passes 'strictly separated … what keeps junctions clean'; only ward interiors cached; walls/towers after wards) and §1.1 ('cache per ward'); profile-neighbourhood §7 (NG closes seams between adjacent shadow quads with a ½-px same-colour stroke).

claim: Label fitting depends on the host's text engine, so model hashes differ across browsers and between UI and headless
claim_full: S13 is a model stage whose F-LABEL rungs depend on text width at the minimum size and on screen-space collisions per LOD; text width comes from the host engine (different shaping in Chromium, Gecko, WebKit; headless Node ships no canvas), so near-threshold labels take different rungs per platform and the model hash differs — O2 (a) and O11 (f) 'headless hash = UI hash' cannot both hold while labels are in the hash, and screen space makes the model viewport/DPR-dependent.
required_change: Either fit labels from font metrics parsed from the bundled OFL fonts (advances + kerning in world units at a declared size) with world-space collision per LOD band, never the host text engine; or exclude label placement from the model hash (derived, cached view data; only pinned/edited placements are model data); state which and test headless vs browser hashes on the golden suite.
evidence: ARCH §9 (screen-space rbush per LOD; 0 collisions invariant), §5.2 F-LABEL, §2.7 Label entity, §6.2 model hash, §1.7 (Node target; @napi-rs/canvas / resvg dev-only 'never shipped'), §15.2 O2 (a), O11 (f).

claim: Stage-2 rule (3) forbids the geometry NG close-ups are made of
claim_full: PART II rule (3) 'no new street end is placed on a shared edge' forbids the geometry NG close-ups consist of: NG cuts end on existing roads (361/361) and ring-template radials run on to the hood edge — inside a PLAT district that edge is the shared boundary street — so bent-cut refinement cannot touch boundary blocks and RingFabric radials cannot reach the boundary; the base's own S8 already ends cuts on district-boundary spines.
required_change: Replace rule (3) with a seam amendment: a close-up may add T-junctions on shared boundary spines, each recorded as a new portal in both districts' SeamContracts and inserted with splitThrough (GEO-1) so the shared spine stays one chain; only the neighbour's corridor and junction wedge are re-derived, never its plots; SeamReport counts added portals; test a ring close-up with radials to the boundary and byte-identical neighbour plots.
evidence: ARCH II.1 rule (3), SeamContract (sharedGeometry 'ownedByBase'), II.2 RingFabric, §4.6 (cuts end on the L1 face's spines), §2.2 rule 1. profile-neighbourhood BG-2 item 6 (every junction on an earlier-drawn road, 361/361), RA-4 ('no rim road: streets simply stop at the edge'; 'The radial streets run on to the edge').

claim: The floating-point lint is a short denylist and misses `
claim_full: The determinism lint forbids only Math.sin/cos/tan/atan2/exp/log/pow, random, Date, performance; it misses the ** operator (same approximated exponentiation as pow — S1's width law acc^0.4 invites it), Math.hypot/asin/acos/atan/cbrt/expm1/log1p/log2/log10/sinh/cosh/tanh, and the adopted geometry/noise libraries, which are never scanned.
required_change: Make the lint an allowlist (Math.abs/floor/ceil/round/trunc/sign/min/max/sqrt/imul/clz32/fround plus arithmetic operators), ban ** except with literal small-integer exponents, and run the same scan over vendored dependency sources with a pinned-version audit.
evidence: ARCH §6.5 (3), D-23, §4.2 S1 (3) (w = w0·acc^0.4), §14 dependency rules, §17 (simplex-noise 'determinism verified'). The ECMA-262 approximation status is general spec knowledge (PLAUSIBLE, not re-read).

claim: "Areas are exact in doubles" holds per product, not per sum; ring orientation must not depend on it
claim_full: 'Areas exact in doubles' holds per product, not for shoelace sums: at the METROPOLIS frame sums stay below 2^53 only up to ≈ 11 000 vertices, and at the declared 2^23 range invariant only 64; ring-orientation or sliver decisions read from such sums are float topology decisions §3.2 (3) forbids.
required_change: Take ring orientation from orient2d at the lowest-leftmost vertex; compute areas relative to the bbox corner or with compensated/BigInt accumulation above a vertex-count threshold; state the bound in §3.2.
evidence: ARCH §2.1 ('products of two bounded 32-bit values are exact'), §3.2 (1), (3). Arithmetic: |x|,|y| ≤ 6.4e5 cm → term ≤ 8.2e11 → n < 9.0e15/8.2e11 ≈ 11 000; at 2^23, term ≤ 2^47 → n < 64.

claim: The authoring boundary neither resamples strokes nor lets a user draw an island
claim_full: Drawn strokes are not resampled before insertChain (60 Hz pointer samples a few cm apart → E_MIN_EDGE on ordinary strokes); drawWater takes one ring and rejects overlapping shapes, so an island cannot be drawn (FTG's documented method is two intersecting ocean shapes); drawBoundary takes arbitrary polygons although district boundaries are 'always spine edges'.
required_change: Resample strokes at the authoring boundary to ≥ minEdge with a topology check; let drawWater take several rings composed by boolean union plus a subtracting land brush; define drawBoundary as snapping to the nearest spine chain or as invisible district_bound L1 edges, and say which.
evidence: ARCH §7.1 draw events, §7.2 (validation: simple, not overlapping), §7.4 drawing-tools row, §2.2 rule 1. FTG 153121107 (ftg-posts-c §2.12): draw 'two ocean shapes … (and those ones can intersect)'; a single self-intersecting shape 'broke some of the logic in the server'.

claim: Quantised anchors flip under 1 cm upstream shifts, and the on-edge anchor tie-break is unstated
claim_full: Anchors are quantised (building centroid to a 1 m cell, quantised frontage offset), so a 1 cm upstream shift (re-snap, neighbour's kerb, splitThrough) flips the cell for ≈ 1–2 % of buildings, superseding ids and orphaning pins/assignments; the tie-break when a split line passes exactly through an anchor point is unstated.
required_change: Match anchors with hysteresis (keep the id if the new centroid lies within 0.5 m of the old anchor) by nearest neighbour with an id tie-break; state the on-edge rule (face left of the directed cut keeps the id); fixture: 1 cm perturbations keep ≥ 99.9 % of ids.
evidence: ARCH §2.1 anchor rule, §2.2 rule 2 ('the part containing the entity's anchor point keeps the id'), §6.3, §7.4 (orphaned assignments). Arithmetic: P(flip) ≈ shift/cell per axis = 1 cm / 100 cm.

claim: Minimum-feature tolerances differ between writers and invariants
claim_full: Minimum-feature rules conflict: insertChain rejects < 25 cm (minEdge), the invariant checks only 'no edge below the weld tolerance' (5 cm), O4 (e) counts sub-weld edges, and F-CORRIDOR tests '0 faces below minEdge' (a length applied to a face); Clipper outputs, offsets, smoothing and warp bypass insertChain and can leave 5–25 cm edges that the invariant accepts and later stages mishandle.
required_change: Enforce one minimum-edge rule in every writer (boolean, offset, smoothing and warp adapters included) and check the invariant at the same value; express face floors as minimum width and area, not minEdge.
evidence: ARCH §2.2 lattice and rule 2, §3.1 (booleans 're-snapped and re-welded'; skeleton pre-clean), §5.2 F-CORRIDOR test, §5.3, §15.2 O4 (e).

claim: S1 river construction: loops, unbounded carving, and vanishing islands
claim_full: S1's meander term can loop the river course onto itself (unintended islets, crossing sites on overlaps); carving the terrain to keep the bed monotonic has no depth bound (a meander on a hillside becomes a trench); a requested river island vanishes when the branch runs within the channels' half-widths.
required_change: Bound meander offsets by half the control spacing and test course simplicity; cap carve depth with an F-RIVER re-route rung; require branch separation ≥ (w_main + w_branch)/2 + minimum islet width, else report the island as not built.
evidence: ARCH §4.2 S1 (3) (Chaikin-smoothed control polyline with alternating offsets; terrain carved to the course), S1 (4) (branch rejoins after k cells), §5.3 (requested features present or reported).

claim: S5's separation rule covers only parallel spines
claim_full: S5 enforces minimum separation only from parallel spines, so proposals may run parallel to shorelines, the stage boundary or wall lines at any distance, leaving strips thinner than the smallest plot depth that S10 cannot fill.
required_change: Apply the regime separation (at least minimum block depth + half a corridor) to shores, wall setback bands and the stage boundary as well as to spines.
evidence: ARCH §4.4 legality list; §4.8 setback band; §4.7 granularity depths (12–60 m).

claim: Wall bands and towers straddle the L1 wall edge, and wall→road conversion has no clearance rule
claim_full: Wall bands and glacis are declared L3 faces but straddle the L1 wall edge (as do towers centred on L1 vertices), breaking nesting; wallToWay turns the band into a ring-road corridor wider than band + setback, overlapping plots and footprints outside the old wall with no clearance rule.
required_change: Model band, glacis, towers and gatehouses as FaceRef unions of per-side parts (like corridors); give wallToWay a clearance rule (re-cut plots along the new corridor keeping ids where anchors survive; demolish footprints that no longer fit, with lifecycle events).
evidence: ARCH §2.2 rule 1 (L3 includes wall bands, glacis), §2.7 Enceinte.band / Tower.vertex, §4.8, §4.11 wallToWay, §15.2 O8 (g) ('wall → road keeps plot ids').

claim: Label spines on holed faces are undefined
claim_full: Area-label spines use 'the longest path of the hole-aware straight skeleton of the simplified face'; water bodies with islets and woods with clearings have cyclic skeletons, where 'longest path' is undefined (and exponential in general), and the non-topology-preserving pre-simplification can make a hole cross the outer ring.
required_change: Define the spine for holed faces (longest path in a clearance-weighted spanning tree of the skeleton, or the medial-axis fallback) and simplify with a topology-preserving simplifier.
evidence: ARCH §9 (area labels for districts, water bodies, woods), §4.5 (districts have no holes), §3.1 skeleton and curves rows, §13.1 ('a tree').

claim: 3-D export: coplanar ground surfaces z-fight, and a river is not a plane
claim_full: glTF exports a terrain heightfield mesh, water planes and building meshes; ground faces draped as separate surfaces over the terrain z-fight (FTG's 3-D problem), and a river 'water plane' cannot follow a descending bed.
required_change: Export the ground as one planar partition (the plat's leaf faces, finest committed level per region, each once) draped on the terrain; export rivers as sloped surfaces following the bed profile (or stepped planes per reach).
evidence: ARCH §11 3-D row, §8.4. FTG T-17 (ftg-posts-b): coplanar displaced texture layers fought until upper polygons were subtracted from lower ones so 'nothing will render on top of each other'.

claim: Control continuity is asserted over decisions that are inherently discrete
claim_full: §7.8 demands continuous controls with 'no jump > ε between adjacent steps', but the design's own expansion example contains a threshold (joinMax += round(wealthLevel · 2)) and every downstream geometric stop rule is discrete (OBB-band stop test, 2.5° straight/bent test, minimum widths, ladder rungs), so a small step can flip a top-level cut on a golden seed; the sweep either fails or ε is tuned to pass.
required_change: State continuity statistically (monotone/continuous in expectation over N seeds per step with a per-seed tolerance); make expansion rows continuous (fractional joinMax as a probability, no round); derive ε from measured per-seed variance.
evidence: ARCH §7.8, §7.7 expansion example, §4.6 steps 1, 3, 5, §13.2 control sweeps.

claim: A bent cut that continues across a street bounding another district writes into that district's batch
claim_full: A bent cut 'may continue across an existing lower-or-equal-class street when collinear within 6°'; when that street bounds another district (S5 also grows lanes), the continuation writes the other district's faces inside this district's S8 batch, breaking per-district atomicity, the worker merge rule and per-district reroll isolation, and making the result depend on district order.
required_change: Forbid continuation across district-boundary edges, or make such a cut a two-district transaction with a canonical order recorded in both SeamContracts.
evidence: ARCH §4.6 step 6, §4.1 (S8 one batch per district; merge protocol 'no shared-edge writes inside a pool'), §4.4 (S5 grows lanes 15–25 m), II.4 (per-district reroll isolation).

claim: One id string is both the address and the stream key; it breaks under re-parenting, recycles dead ids, and encodes JOIN membership
claim_full: One hierarchical id string `<kind>:<parent path>/<n>`, minted from a per-parent creation-order counter, is both the address every edit, lock, assignment, pin, household and label points at and the key of the entity's random streams. It cannot survive the re-parenting the design itself performs (drawBoundary re-runs S6, district merge/split, outskirtToDistrict, epoch district extension, a locked plot outliving a district regenerate): the re-parented entity either takes a new path (locks, assignments and renames orphan) or keeps a path that lies, after which the parent's counter mints the same string again (duplicate id, batch abort). Fresh ids are 'minted afresh' at their creation position and a revision suffix is used 'only on collision with a locked or edited id', so a superseded id that was assigned, pin-hosting, labelled or housing a household is recycled to an unrelated entity and every reference silently re-binds. JOINed plot ids encode their member list, so a prosperity brush or an epoch that changes a join set changes the ids of exactly the manor, inn and institution plots most likely to carry assignments.
required_change: Separate address from lineage. Address id: opaque, document-scoped, minted once from a per-kind high-water counter persisted in the document, never reused (tombstones with supersededBy), parent held as a field and never parsed from the string. Carry-over: every re-derivation (regenerate, Adjust, template replacement, migration, epoch) matches new entities to old by anchor (GEO-34 hysteresis plus a class-compatibility check) and hands over the old address id, including across a change of parent. Stream key: a lineage key (parent lineage key + local creation index + reroll, attempt, epoch) recorded in Provenance and kept by a carried-over entity so its draws do not change. JOIN ids follow the anchor rule. One collision rule: a fresh id never equals a live or tombstoned id. Exports carry address ids and a supersedes table. B-EDIT fixtures with drawBoundary, district merge and split, outskirtToDistrict, regenerate around a lock and an id-recycling case: 0 duplicate ids, 0 silent re-binds.
evidence: ARCH §2.1 (id format, anchor rule, collision rule, JOIN id), §6.3, §6.1 (path = stage/entity id/concern), §7.2 (locks as fixed inputs; drawn boundaries before S6), §7.4 (orphans), §4.11 (outskirtToDistrict; districts extend), §4.5 (merge floor), §4.7 S10 (7), §2.8 (single LifecycleState). Brief, ASSIGNMENT HOOK: ids 'that survive regeneration and edits'; one-page: 'edits are saved as a list of events on stable ids, they survive regeneration and version upgrades'. IMPROVEMENTS O9 design idea: 'locked and edited entities are never mutated'. FTG 65223067 and 66499838 (ftg-posts-a rows 1–2): an id-model change 'requires destroying all existing towns'; D-12, D-13 and D-15 price reversal 'high after M1'.

claim: Lazy per-district derivation of S10–S14 makes the model depend on the order districts are viewed
claim_full: S10–S14 are 'lazy per district after the first paint' and METROPOLIS 'relies on' it, but S10b siting fills plots town-wide 'in descending score with capacity accounting' and reconciles by JOINing plots in the affinity or next-best district, S10's claims-first step needs siting's decision before a district's plots are cut, the F-CUT substitution rung reads 'the roster's largest unplaced class', S13 collisions and names are town-wide, and the prosperity drivers include kernels around tanneries and institutions that exist only after siting. The order in which districts are first viewed therefore decides which plot hosts the guildhall, which plots are joined, which block is substituted and which label wins: two users (or the UI and the headless CLI) get different towns from one seed.
required_change: Write a laziness contract: a stage may be lazy only if its output for district D is a pure function of eager upstream state and D's own sub-stream, reading no other district's lazy output and writing nothing outside D. Split S10b into an eager town-level allocation after S9 (demand per class to districts and blocks, claims and JOIN decisions at block granularity) and a lazy per-district placement that honours it; move institution-dependent prosperity kernels to the allocation or to a declared eager second field pass; F-CUT reads the allocation, not live roster state; S13 either eager per LOD or view data outside the model hash (LC-17, GEO-29). Define the model hash over the fully derived model; CI derives districts in random permutations and requires identical hashes.
evidence: ARCH §4.1 bullet 1, §4.7 S10 (3) and S10b, §5.2 F-SITING and F-CUT rows, §4.5 driver list, §9 collision per LOD, §12 ('METROPOLIS relies on lazy per-district derivation of S10–S13'), §6.2 (pure function), O2 (a), O11 (f) 'headless hash = UI hash', one-page 'The same seed always gives the same town on every machine'. MFCG and NG build the whole model before drawing and FTG generates in one server pass (_critic-ftg F20; roadlength100 README), so the hazard is new with the lazy tier.

claim: Stream paths embed creation-order ids, so upstream changes reshuffle every descendant; the golden protocol's byte-identity claim is false
claim_full: Stream paths embed creation-order ids, so any change that alters an upstream stage's output (a new branch type in S5, a fix that consumes one more heading draw) renumbers districts, blocks and plots below it and moves every downstream draw although the downstream code is unchanged. 'Adding a feature later does not reshuffle existing maps', 'feature growth without reshuffling' and 'stages untouched by a release stay byte-identical … a property rather than a hope' are false as stated; a shift record naming S5 is accompanied by moved goldens in S6–S14, which are either bulk re-signed (an S11 regression landing in the same release rides through) or leave CI red.
required_change: Stage-isolated goldens: each stage's golden is the hash of the new stage code run on the previous release's frozen upstream outputs, so only stages whose code or tables changed can differ; end-to-end goldens re-signed only with a cascade record listing every downstream stage that moved and showing through the isolated goldens that each moved only through its inputs; restate the one-page sentence and D-15 to the true scope (independent concerns and later stages do not reshuffle; a geometry change reshuffles its descendants as a declared shift); rely on LC-1's carry-over, not on stream paths, where edited documents need stability.
evidence: ARCH one-page; §6.1 paths (e.g. S11/siteplan/plot:d3/b7/p2/arrangement); §6.3 (already scoped to 'another stage or concern'); §13.3; D-15; D-24; O2 (b), (e). _critic-vg-ng V25: across VG builds 19251041 and 19365073 seed 3131 kept its name and POIs but not its geometry — per-concern streams protect names, nothing protects downstream geometry. vg-posts-b §2.23 (105215836): 1.6.1 'a behaviour-shift release: the same seed would not reproduce a pre-1.6.1 map'.

claim: "Adjust … locality guaranteed" cannot hold for the basic panel's parameters, and O2 (c) is vacuous as defined
claim_full: 'Adjust re-solves with a changed parameter, locality guaranteed' and O2 (c) '≥ 95 % of entities that do not depend on it stay byte-identical' after 'one more gate, coast side west' cannot hold: in PLAT the gate count is an S3 destination list and the coast side an S1 input, so every arterial, growth stage, district seed and id downstream depends on them; the 'do not depend' set is empty and the index vacuous. Nine of the twelve basic-panel controls are consumed in S0–S7. A user who adds a gate to an edited town gets a new town inside the wall with every edit passing through anchor matching, and the dry run validates invariants only, so it never says so.
required_change: Record each parameter's consuming stage in the control registry; promise Adjust locality only for parameters consumed at S10 or later or carrying a spatial scope; for earlier ones the action is 'Re-derive from stage k' with LC-1 carry-over and a dry-run edit-fate report (kept, carried, orphaned — counts and list) the user confirms; restate O2 (c) per parameter class: entities outside the stage-k closure byte-identical 100 %, edited-entity carry-over rate reported, target set after M3 measures it.
evidence: ARCH §7.1, §7.3 (Adjust via the DAG), §7.8 basic panel, §4.2 S3 (gates as destinations), §15.2 O2 (c); IMPROVEMENTS O2 acceptance (c) and its MFCG baseline; profile-mfcg EG2-4 (changing gates re-rolls 'streets, wards, districts, buildings, fields and every name'); IMPROVEMENTS O2 answers: FTG roadLength 60→100 gave 4→3 districts and 17→29 towers.

claim: The failure ladder and "New random" share the `attempt` segment
claim_full: The failure ladder (tier 3: 'retry the same entity with the next ATTEMPT sub-stream; ≤ 3 attempts') and the user's 'New random' ('re-derives the scope with attempt + 1') share one path segment. If a block's committed result came from ladder attempt 1, New random reproduces it exactly (the button does nothing); counted from the committed attempt, rerolls consume the ladder, so the third reroll has no tier-3 retry left and any failure drops to straight cuts or a court substitution; a scope whose blocks sit at different attempts has no single 'attempt + 1', and a relative attempt in the event does not replay.
required_change: Two segments: /reroll=r (user intent, absolute per entity, stored in provenance and in the event as an explicit per-entity map) and /attempt=n (ladder, restarting at 0 for every reroll with the same cap); test that New random always changes its scope or reports 'no alternative within the ladder'.
evidence: ARCH §5.1 tiers, §6.1 'Attempts append /attempt=n', §7.1 four actions, §7.4 regenerate row (log: scope, mode, attempt), §14 stream(concern, entity?, attempt?). profile-mfcg seed chain: MFCG keeps per-ward rerolls independent of its retry stream by Random.save/restore.

claim: Quantile bands with hysteresis, and band-only re-derivation, make prosperity results path-dependent and non-local
claim_full: Prosperity is banded 'by quantiles with hysteresis' while continuous rules interpolate along the value, and a field edit 'regenerates the plots and site plans of the blocks whose band changed, nothing else'. Quantiles are town-relative, so a stroke in one quarter (or an epoch's rich suburb) moves thresholds and re-bands blocks far away; hysteresis makes a band depend on the previous band, so a from-scratch replay and the session disagree; a stroke that moves values inside a band changes what a replay computes (interpolated width, coverage) but re-derives nothing, so the user sees no effect and the next load reports a mismatch. Whether a stroke is absolute or relative, which decides what an epoch does with it, is unstated.
required_change: Bands from absolute, calibratable thresholds in the table (or quantile thresholds computed once and stored as recipe data, changed only by an explicit event); hysteresis keyed to the entity's recorded band so replay reproduces it; a field edit re-derives every block whose interpolated inputs moved beyond a declared tolerance, the same tolerance on replay; strokes declared relative (Δ composited over the driver field, clamped once) and their epoch behaviour stated.
evidence: ARCH §4.5 (banding, interpolation, 'editable as a brush layer', epochs keep strokes), §4.7 granularity table interpolated, §7.2, §7.3 oracle, §4.11, §2.9 K-3; O18 (g) perturbation ≥ 95 % outside, O18 (i) 'edits replay'. Arithmetic example in §3.

claim: Coarse-level edits have no local re-derivation operator
claim_full: 'L(n+1) = refine_n(L(n)); an edit at level n invalidates only the finer faces under the touched faces' holds from L1 faces down, but L1 is not a per-L0-face refinement: S4 routes between destinations across the frame, S5 grows a town-wide queue, S6 grows districts across faces and S7 traces a whole enceinte. §7.1 makes terrain, water outlines, river control points, ways, districts, walls and gates edit targets, and the terrain brush inherits a 'blocks whose band changed' rule that has no meaning for terrain. A terrain or river edit therefore either re-runs the pipeline from S1 (the town re-rolls; 'the rest of the town is byte-identical' fails) or leaves an inconsistent model (a bridge over land, a road ending at the new bank, footprints in the new channel — the hard 'water ∩ footprints = ∅' invariant aborts the batch and no ladder row covers it).
required_change: Specify a local operator per coarse stage with pinned boundaries: S1 edits treat water as locked unless the edit targets water; S4 re-routes only arterials whose corridors meet the edit region, with endpoints and outside spines pinned; S5 regrows only inside the affected coarse faces with their boundary spines pinned; S6 re-grows only districts touching the region; S7 re-traces only the affected wall run. The dry run shows the effective region and the edit fates (LC-4, LC-8); where no local operator exists the edit is declared 're-derive from Sk' with carry-over, never presented as local; B-EDIT adds terrain and river-control-point sequences.
evidence: ARCH §2.2 rule 4, §7.3, §7.1 targets, §7.2 (field rule; drawn constraints before S1, S4, S6, S7), §4.2 S1 (3) (rivers by descent, terrain carved to the course), §4.1 (S4 and S5 one batch per stage), §5.3. References regenerate only below the coarse level: MFCG rerolls wards inside fixed streets (profile-mfcg seed chain, save/restore); FTG regenerates lots with roads kept, and its users still see regenerated areas 'denser than the original' (ftg-posts-c §2.20; 157283634).

claim: The fate of edits inside a regenerate scope is undefined; overrides follow ids to other entities or vanish
claim_full: Only locked or pinned entities are protected from regeneration; the fate of edits on other entities inside a regenerate scope is unspecified, and IMPROVEMENTS O9's 'locked and edited entities are never mutated' was dropped. Under the anchor rule an edited but unlocked entity either keeps its id because its anchor cell did not move, and its setAttr overrides (name, use, class, heights, roof) are re-applied to what is now a different building, or it is superseded and its edits vanish (orphaned, or silently re-bound per LC-1). Pin hosts, labels, assignments and pinned people inside the scope are in the same position, and so are entities replaced by a stage-2 template.
required_change: Restore O9's rule: an edited attribute implicitly pins that attribute and the entity's existence against Regenerate and New random unless the user chooses 'discard edits in scope'; the dry run lists every edited, assigned, pin-hosting, labelled or people-pinned entity in the effective scope with its fate (kept as a fixed input; carried to its anchor-matched successor after a class-compatibility check; discarded by an explicit supersede event) and shows the effective scope (the covering faces, which can exceed the drawn area); overrides never transfer by id alone.
evidence: ARCH §7.2, §7.3 ('discard every unpinned finer entity'), §7.4 setAttr row ('an input override at the stage that would compute it') and regenerate row, §2.1 anchor rule, II.1 rule 4 and SeamReport.superseded, §2.7 Pin.host; IMPROVEMENTS O9 design idea and acceptance (b), (e). FTG: bulk regenerate 'will delete any residents' and 'cannot be undone' (ftg-posts-c §2.20); users refuse to re-roll a district because of 'custom locations I already baked in' (IMPROVEMENTS O9, 120828892); MFCG churches 'used to disappear after rerolling a ward' (IMPROVEMENTS O9).

claim: Assignments override locks, dispersed re-solves move untouched placements, and assignments enter by two paths
claim_full: 'Order of precedence at S10–S11: assignment > lock > …' lets a later or host assignment overwrite an entity the user locked; a dispersed assignment whose one member is superseded is re-solved from its criteria, and the greedy max-min solver then moves the members in districts nobody touched; assignments enter both as recipe data (applied by S10's claims-first step) and as assign events (applied afterwards), so the same assignment gives different towns by path; whether epochs re-solve dispersed assignments is unstated.
required_change: Precedence lock > assignment > user-drawn geometry > rules; a targeted assignment on a locked entity is a dry-run conflict; the dispersed solver excludes locked entities; re-solve only the unmapped members with mapped placements as fixed points; one path (recipe assignments are sugar for assign events at log position 0, and every assign event triggers the same claims-first re-derivation for its scope); epochs keep placed members and add members only when count or criteria change.
evidence: ARCH §7.7 (precedence; PlacementSolver), §7.4 assign row ('criteria replay if an id is unmapped'), §2.9 recipe.assignments, §4.2 S0 Blueprint, §4.7 S10 (3), §5.2 F-EDIT, §6.4 (&a=<assignment hash>), §4.11. Brief, ASSIGNMENT HOOK: the assignment 'takes precedence over the generator's own class rules' — over rules, not over the user's locks.

claim: Drawn constraints are hoisted before their stage on replay but applied at their log position interactively
claim_full: Drawn ways, water, walls, greens and boundaries are 'inserted before the stage that would create the class', while every other event applies in log order to the state at its position. Interactively a drawn way enters a finished town and the area re-derives with carry-over and revision suffixes; on replay (K-3 background verification, undo beyond the 8-snapshot ring, migration) it is hoisted to S4 and the whole town is generated around it with creation-order ids. Any later edit on an entity created by the session's local re-derivation addresses an id the replay mints differently: it is orphaned or silently re-bound, every such document fails verification on every load, and migration loses the edit.
required_change: One replay semantics, an ordered fold: each event applies to the state after its predecessors, and a drawn constraint re-runs its class's stage for the affected scope at its log position — the same code path interactively and on replay (GEO-11 asks this for weld order); hoisting survives only as an explicit 'rebase' that rewrites the recipe and shows a diff like a migration; CI requires replay(recipe, log) = session hash on B-EDIT sequences that mix draw events with later attribute edits.
evidence: ARCH §7.2, §7.4 drawing row ('inserted as constraints before the stage…'; migrate 'replay inserts the same geometry'), §2.9 K-3 policy, §14 EditEngine.replay(recipe, edits), §6.2, §7.3 oracle.

claim: Epochs are not events in the ordered log
claim_full: Epochs are not events: grow() writes doc.epochs, the EditEvent union has no epoch kind, EditEngine.replay(recipe, edits) takes no epochs, and the recipe carries a separate circumstances timeline. The order of edits relative to epochs is lost (edits to epoch-2 entities replay against epoch 0 and orphan), a multi-epoch document cannot be re-derived for K-3 verification, an epoch cannot be undone, and a migration re-runs the recipe so epoch 0 re-rolls under the new version while the later epochs were derived from states the new version never persisted — the 200-year history does not survive an upgrade.
required_change: {t:'epoch', epoch, inputs} is an EditEvent in the ordered log (the recipe's timeline only schedules such events); EpochRecord = {log index, inputs, post-epoch hash}; replay folds epochs in order; undo of an epoch restores the pre-epoch snapshot; a multi-epoch document migrates by replaying the whole ordered log with a per-epoch diff, or is pinned to its version (LC-14); M4's exit test replays a document with interleaved edits and two epochs to the session hash.
evidence: ARCH §4.11, §2.9 (Document: epochs, circumstances, snapshot optional), §7.1 union, §14 EditEngine, §7.5, §16 M4 (the incremental path arrives after M3's log), D-25. Brief, EVOLUTION: 'epoch N+1 is derived from epoch N's persisted state, the inputs and the seed's epoch sub-stream … every change traces to a recorded event'.

claim: An epoch re-solves the global fields while promising survivors are not re-rolled
claim_full: An epoch re-solves the town-wide fields ('the fields are re-solved with the previous field as a prior') and then re-derives S8–S13 'on new or changed faces only' while promising that 'nothing that survives is re-rolled because its stream path is unchanged'. The re-solved field changes the context vector of surviving plots everywhere: if their faces count as changed, S10–S11 re-derive them with unchanged streams but new inputs (a re-roll by another name; M4's '0 re-rolled survivors' fails); if not, survivors keep stale context and a later 'Regenerate (keep settings)' on an untouched block re-derives it with the new field, so the faithful action changes a block nobody asked to change. Delta demand plus global siting have the same two outcomes for survivors' uses.
required_change: Survivors keep their built state across epochs; a field change acts on them only through explicit, rate-limited transformation events chosen by rules (densify, subdivide, amalgamate, decay, rebuild) triggered by band crossings beyond a hysteresis and drawn from …/epoch=e streams; each entity records the inputs of its last derivation (field sample, band, table versions) so 'Regenerate (keep)' reproduces it, and re-deriving with current inputs is the explicit Adjust; siting across epochs places only delta demand on new or transformed plots.
evidence: ARCH §4.11, §4.5 (the field moved by epochs), §7.2, §7.3, §4.7 S10b, §16 M4 exit, D-25; brief EVOLUTION (districts densifying or decaying as recorded events; nothing that survives is re-rolled) and PROSPERITY ('the evolution stage moves the field over time').

claim: Choosing the snapshot (or keeping the old model) leaves a document whose later undo, migration and verification switch back silently
claim_full: On a hash mismatch 'the user chooses the snapshot or the replay', and at an upgrade 'the user may keep the old materialised model', but nothing rebases the document: its recipe and log still replay to the other state. Every later load reports the same mismatch; undo beyond the 8-snapshot ring is 'rebuilt by replay' and silently returns the replay's town; the next migration discards the chosen snapshot; a kept old model whose version leaves the replay window can no longer be regenerated faithfully and later edits run the new pipeline on old-version entities under one generatorVersion field; edits made while a METROPOLIS verification is still running are replayed onto another state if the user then picks the replay.
required_change: A rebase event: choosing the snapshot (or keeping an old model) compacts the document — the chosen state becomes the new base with its hash, the log restarts after it, replay starts from the base snapshot, and the document records that it is not seed-reproducible before that point; undo below the rebase uses the base; a kept old model pins the replay version (LC-14); edits wait until verification finishes or the user chooses.
evidence: ARCH §2.9 persistence policy, §7.4 regenerate row (k = 8; older snapshots rebuilt by replay), §7.5, §12 memory, J-8, D-21.

claim: Migration: unspecified id mapping, silent mis-binding, orphan locks that no longer protect, and no mechanism for "the last N versions"
claim_full: Migration re-applies the log 'on the id-mapped model', but the mapping is unspecified; with creation-order ids the new version mints the same strings for different entities, so string equality mis-binds edits silently instead of reporting orphans (O9 (e) fails without a report). An orphaned lock is 'listed … with its last geometry' but not re-imposed, so the locked building is replaced by whatever the new version draws. 'The last N minor versions stay replayable' — the only mechanism behind 'permalinks never silently change' — has no stated shipping mechanism in a browser library without a server, no N, no rule for major versions and no milestone; an upgrade is not an event, so it cannot be undone after commit.
required_change: Specify the mapping: old snapshot entities matched to the new model by kind, anchor, class family and overlap above a threshold, with LC-1 carry-over; unmatched edits are reported orphans, never string-matched; an orphaned lock re-imposes its last geometry as a user-drawn constraint unless the user drops it; the upgrade is an undoable event keeping the pre-upgrade snapshot; define retention: an output version that bumps only with a declared shift, old output versions of the model packages kept as versioned tree-shakable modules for a stated window, documents outside it open as frozen snapshots (view, export, rebase per LC-13); build and test it in M3 (replay goldens under N−1 and N−2).
evidence: ARCH §7.5, §7.4 lock and assign migrate cells, §2.9, §6.4, D-21, §16 (no milestone); _critic-vg-ng V25 (same seed, 29 → 24 buildings across builds); vg-posts-b §2.34 (VG stores house marks in its permalinks from 1.6.5 [STATED, 117634240]; the numbering is creation order [INFERRED]); FTG 65223067/66499838 (towns destroyed by an id-model change) and 151265004 ('no way to automatically regenerate settlements with these features').

claim: The recipe and the permalink omit model-affecting inputs; an assignment hash cannot reproduce assignments; `&doc=<id>` needs a server that does not exist
claim_full: The model reads more than the recipe and the permalink carry. §6.2 says model = G(version, seed, params, assignments, edits), but §7.6's effective parameters include userGlobal and documentOverrides, §7.7 adds intent, character and circumstances, and S10b has two entry points. The permalink carries v, s, z, a params delta from a preset, the preset id, an assignment hash (which cannot reproduce assignments), and &doc=<id> (which resolves nowhere: no server, sync deferred); table and style versions are separate axes not in the link, and preset=<id> resolves to a user-edited preset on the author's machine. A shared link therefore reproduces another town without warning, against D-21.
required_change: Define the canonical recipe as every model-affecting input: seed, rung, the full effective parameter delta over the shipped defaults of the pinned table versions (userGlobal and documentOverrides copied into the document at creation and folded in), intent, character, circumstances, entry mode, assignments inline, table-version pins, output version; the permalink is the compressed canonical recipe (or refuses and offers a file); &doc= only when a resolver is configured; the style version in the link for pixel identity; CI tests permalink → recipe → permalink identity and permalink hash = session hash; the app warns when a link cannot carry the document.
evidence: ARCH §2.9, §6.2, §6.4, §7.6, §7.7, §4.7 S10b (entry points), §1.7 ('no server'), deferrals ('a sync service'), D-21. MFCG 102377277: 'No manual changes made to a map are encoded into its URL' and a round trip 'subtly changed the city geometry' (mfcg-posts-b §2.21); MFCG's URL has no version key (profile-mfcg §2); PS legend edits are not in its permalink (watabou-extra-a §2.21).

claim: "A person is pinned once seen" turns reading into writing, and pinned people dangle when their household moves
claim_full: 'A person is pinned once seen or edited (FTG's rule)' turns viewing into a persistent write: the document (and the hash, if pins are model data) depends on what the user looked at, the headless API and the UI diverge, browsing the gazetteer fills the edit log and the undo stack and overflows the 2 KB inline-log permalink. FTG's documented rule locks details on edit, not on view. Pinned people reference households that are re-derived by plot regeneration and by siting's reconcile, so they dangle or attach to households of another size; §7.4 has no people row; people have no time argument, so survivors of an epoch keep their ages for decades.
required_change: Pins come only from an explicit user action or an edit (FTG's rule); what a user has seen is per-user view state outside the document; a person key = (household lineage id under LC-1, member ordinal, birth epoch) with an ageing rule per epoch; §7.4 gains a people row (regenerate: households with pinned or edited people are fixed inputs or re-homed by rule with an event; migrate: orphaned people reported); O7 (g) tested under table edits as a declared shift for unpinned people.
evidence: ARCH §10.3, §4.7 S10b ('pinned once seen'), §2.7 Person and Household, §7.4 (no people row), §14 ContentProvider.people vs derivePerson(seed, id); research/ftg-docs/useSettlements__settings.md (FTG saves 'only a few key details … per person. The rest is generated when the person is selected. When a person is manually edited, those generated details are locked in'), ftg-docs-params §3.10; FTG regenerate 'will delete any residents and may update other people' (ftg-posts-c §2.20); IMPROVEMENTS O9 ('people are reconciled … rather than deleted').

claim: Every local regeneration re-runs names and labels for the whole town
claim_full: After any scoped regeneration the design 're-run[s] only the label and display stages globally', but S13 is a model stage (names and Label entities, a hard 0-collision invariant, the model hash). A block reroll moves label candidates and collision outcomes across the town and can change names conditioned on the model or resolved for uniqueness outside the scope, so O2 (b) 'rerolling one block changes nothing outside it', O2 (d) and O9 (b) fail for labels and possibly names; name uniqueness is unspecified (resolved in creation order, a new street steals 'Mill Lane' and a street elsewhere is renamed); moveLabel is declared outside the model hash while Label is a model entity.
required_change: Decide the status of label placement together with GEO-29: view data derived per LOD from the model plus pinned placements (outside the model hash and the byte-identity claims), or S13 re-run only inside the regenerated region plus a declared collision halo; names are per-entity draws with deterministic uniqueness that never renames an existing entity (the new entity re-draws); feature-conditioned names re-evaluated only inside the scope; test: a block reroll changes 0 names outside it.
evidence: ARCH §7.3, §4.10, §9 (collision; names conditioned on the model), §2.7 Label, §7.4 setLayer/setStyle/moveLabel row, §5.3; O2 (b), (d); O9 (b); O13 (e) 'edited names persist 100 %'.

claim: Stage-2 close-ups have no persistence status
claim_full: Stage-2 close-ups have no persistence status. A 'bent-cut' close-up refines inside faces and returns blocks, ways, plots, buildings, greens, pins and labels; the neighbourhood tier is 'generated lazily per district tile'; stage-3 compositions are 'lazily generated, stored only when edited'.
