If refinements enter the model, the town (and its city-LOD footprints, which the owner wants shown at every zoom) differs before and after a district is opened and between users; if they do not, edits to close-up entities (move a well, rename a close-up lane, lock a close-up house) have no create, persist, regenerate or migrate path, and the 'same kind, new seed per district with locks' workflow has nothing to lock.
required_change: State that a close-up is a pure function of the district's committed base state, its sub-seed, strategy and params (deterministic whether computed eagerly or lazily), held as a derived refinement level outside the base hash until its first edit, after which its edits are events on close-up ids anchored like base entities; a base re-derivation of the district re-derives its close-up with carry-over and reports orphans; city-LOD footprints read the same source at every zoom, so a close-up that changes footprints is a model change with its own event.
evidence: ARCH II.1 (rules 2 and 4; NeighbourhoodResult; SeamReport), II.4, II.5, §8.6, §2.6, §7.4 (no close-up row); brief PRODUCT SCOPE: stage 2 designed 'to the depth needed to guarantee the base's model supports it'; stage 3 'those footprint shapes are what shows at every zoom, including the city view'.

claim: The build plan ships permalinks and goldens at M1, the shift protocol at M4, and version retention nowhere
claim_full: The build plan ships 'permalink … goldens v0' at M1, adds at M2 the prosperity field, the full granularity law, siting, compounds, greenery and the suburb regime (each changes every M1 town for the same seed), and brings the declared-shift protocol and per-stage hashes only at M4; no milestone builds the N-version replay. From M1 to M4 every same-seed change rides without a shift record, the owner's side-by-side seeds (D-5) change between milestones, and M1 permalinks break by design.
required_change: Move the shift record, the output-version stamp and per-stage golden tooling into M1; label pre-M4 permalinks as preview links showing their output version; every milestone's exit lists its declared shifts; add version retention to M3 with an exit test (LC-14).
evidence: ARCH §16 (M1, M2, M4 rows), §13.3, D-5, D-21, D-24 (tooling priced 'trivial'); §13.3 quoting owner non-negotiable 10 ('a same-seed output change is never let ride silently').

claim: Render-time instances are keyed by LOD band and cannot be edited
claim_full: Decoration draws from style streams 'keyed by entity id and LOD band at render time and is never stored', so tree, scatter and roof-detail positions differ between district and neighbourhood LOD and between exports at different LODs (a VTT scene vs a print), contrary to 'geometry never changes with zoom'; and an individual tree, stall or roof detail — a generated element — has no edit event, although every generated element must be editable with edits that persist and survive regeneration; any edit to a greenery face re-rolls every tree on it.
required_change: One decoration stream per entity; LOD subsets as prefixes of a progressive ordered sample so each coarser band is a subset of the finer one; an instance-override event {t:'instance', entity, ordinal or point, op: add, move, remove, restyle} replayed as geometry after regeneration (ordinals re-matched by position); B-ZOOM checks instance positions identical across the bands where they exist.
evidence: ARCH §6.1, §2.7 Greenery.treeStream, §4.9 (trees at render), §8.1, §13.4 (B-ZOOM no pops), §7.1 ('every generated element is a target', owner amendment 5). FTG forest fills are render-time and their determinism untested (_critic-ftg §2 and §6 item 4); IMPROVEMENTS O2 answers: MFCG tree crowns and gable counts differ between two renders of one city.

claim: Table-edit invalidation by cited rows is too narrow
claim_full: 'A rule change invalidates exactly the entities whose Provenance.rules cite that row' misses entities that consulted the table without citing the changed row: a weighted draw depends on every weight, an interpolated rule on both bracketing rows, a band lookup on the thresholds, and an inserted row on everything it would now match. Those entities stay stale, the oracle fails, and the implied fallback for a table edit (no spatial scope) is an unstated whole-town re-derivation.
required_change: Provenance cites (table id, hash of the consulted slice): the whole weight vector for weighted draws, the bracketing pair for interpolation, the threshold set for bands; invalidate on slice-hash change; B-EDIT includes weight edits and row insertions; state the fallback.
evidence: ARCH §7.4 editTable row, §6.1 (weighted, deck), §4.7 interpolation, §7.3 (oracle; DAG trusted only where proven), §2.8 Provenance.rules.

claim: JSON-Patch overrides silently retarget after a table update
claim_full: Table and preset overrides are JSON Patch documents, whose pointers address array rows by position; when a shipped table version inserts or reorders rows, an override silently applies to a different row (not 'reported and kept orphaned'). FTG documents the same class: an edited person's hair stored as option index '1' turns red when the option list changes and blank when the option is removed.
required_change: Address rows by stable row keys (keyed maps or a custom patch op) and store the base row's hash with each override; applying to a changed or missing row reports an orphan.
evidence: ARCH §7.1 editTable/editPreset (patch: JsonPatch), §6.4 ('user overrides carry their base version'), §7.4 editTable migrate cell; research/ftg-docs/useSettlements__settings.md (index-stored options).

claim: Caches keyed by entity id serve stale content
claim_full: Derived geometry is 'cached by entity id', lazy stage outputs are 'cached by id' and tiles are re-rasterised 'only when a district's marks change'; the anchor rule keeps ids when content changes (heights or roof setAttr, a regenerated footprint whose centroid stays in its 1 m cell, a table edit), so stale roofs, spines and scatter are served, and marks shared across districts (a boundary street, a label) change without the district's own marks changing.
required_change: Cache key = (id, content revision hash of the entity's inputs, LOD band, style version); invalidation from the closure the locality mechanism already computes.
evidence: ARCH §8.5, §4.1 bullet 1, §2.1 anchor rule.

claim: Duplicated document state
claim_full: The document stores several facts twice without a declared source of truth — locks as a set and as events, preferences as prefs and as editTable/editPreset events, assignments in the recipe and as events, epochs outside the log, and a report with per-stage millisecond timings — so after a migration, an undo or a background verification the copies can disagree and save → load → save byte identity (O9 a) depends on which copy is written.
required_change: Declare locks, prefs, epochs, report and stats as derived caches rebuilt from the log and excluded from the canonical form and the hash, or make them authoritative and drop the duplicate events; timings live outside the canonical document.
evidence: ARCH §2.9 Document, §5.4 (ms per stage), §7.4 lock row ('doc.locks'), §7.6.

claim: Version stamps in the hashed model
claim_full: Provenance stores generatorVersion and tableVersions on every entity and the model hash covers 'the canonical serialisation', so a release that changes no output still changes every entity and every hash; every golden moves each release and LC-3's isolation test cannot pass.
required_change: Hash model content only (geometry, attributes, address ids, lineage keys) and keep version stamps and deps in a separately hashed provenance block.
evidence: ARCH §2.8 Provenance, §6.2, §5.3 ('the model hash recomputed equals the recorded one'), §13.3.

claim: A single-valued lifecycle state drops pins
claim_full: Lifecycle.state is a single value (generated, edited, pinned, assigned, …), so a pin followed by an assign leaves the entity 'assigned' and no longer 'pinned' to any code reading the state, and an edited-then-assigned id becomes recyclable under §6.3's 'locked or edited' guard (LC-1).
required_change: Orthogonal flags (locked, pinned, edited, assigned) plus an existence state (generated, built, altered, converted, demolished); the history stays the event list.
evidence: ARCH §2.8 LifecycleState, §6.3, §7.2.

claim: Two inverses are not inverses
claim_full: Two inverses are not inverses. A brush undo is an 'inverse stroke', which is inexact once values clamp (+0.3 on 0.9 clamps to 1.0; −0.3 gives 0.7). A warp persists 'both the per-vertex displacement and the brush stroke', so after a district-level regenerate or a migration mapped vertices get the recorded displacement and new ones 'sample the stroke field' — but Equalize, Bloat, Pinch and Rotate act on cells, not as displacement fields, so the replayed warp differs from the session and mixes two semantics across one region.
required_change: Strokes kept as a list composited once (clamp at the end), undo removes the stroke; warp replays as the operation (kernel, centre, radius, strength) on the current geometry at its log position (LC-10), per-vertex displacements kept only as a verification record.
evidence: ARCH §7.4 setField and moveVertex/warp rows, §7.1 warp event; _critic.md C4/C5 (Equalize = a cell's angles, Bloat = larger cells).

claim: Enter, clone, document identity and forward compatibility
claim_full: 'Enter = seed + 1' does not say what happens to parameters, intent, locks, edits and assignments (MFCG's Enter drops explicit parameters); the document has no identity, so a clone carries the same ids and a host holding two towns cannot tell their plot:d3/b7/p2 apart; opening a document saved by a newer version in an older embedded library is unspecified (migrations run forward only); §6.1's reference note is imprecise — MFCG's successor seed is the deterministic stream state, what is irreproducible is its size and flags.
required_change: Enter = a new document with seed + 1 and the same recipe without edits, locks and assignments (with a warning when the current document has edits); a document uuid minted at creation, kept on save, re-minted on clone and prefixed to ids at the API boundary; a newer schema opens read-only with a message; correct §6.1's note.
evidence: ARCH §6.1, §2.9, §7.5, §11 (embedding API, bridge); profile-mfcg Explicit-gates addendum ('the value persists through Blueprint.updateURL but is dropped by Enter'; 47063541 'pressing Enter … forgets the number of roads'; seed chain k = 585 in both passes; size and flags from a non-seeded input).

claim: Ids and stream paths are not layer-qualified
claim_full: Ids and stream paths carry no layer segment although each layer has its own plat and sky islands carry districts; a sky district minted district:d3 shares every stream path with ground district:d3 and draws identical numbers (mirrored cut choices); the distinct-key CI test runs on B-CITY, which has no sky layer.
required_change: Add a layer (and island) segment to address ids and lineage keys; include a sky-island fixture in the distinct-key test.
evidence: ARCH §2.1 (layers; ids), §6.1 (paths; distinct-key test), §2.7 SkyIsland, II.1 sky call.

claim: Session state outside the recipe: proxies, "Surprise me", entry mode
claim_full: Three pieces of session state sit outside the recipe: choosing a proxy thumbnail 'continues that seed's pipeline from S5', so if any proxy is computed with a budget-driven simplification (F-BUDGET-TIME, GEO-2) the continued town differs from its permalink replay; 'Surprise me' draws an intent from an unstated source; and S10b's layout-first entry point is not a recipe field.
required_change: Proxies are bit-identical S0–S4 runs, checked by hash when picked; surprise intents come from a seeded intent stream and are written into the recipe; the entry mode is a recipe field.
evidence: ARCH §7.8 proxy thumbnails, §7.1 ('Surprise me'), §4.7 S10b entry points, §5.2 F-BUDGET-TIME.

claim: Host inputs are not required to reach the document
claim_full: Host inputs are not required to reach the document: bridge commands (UPDATE_ENTITY, ASSIGN, REGENERATE) are not stated to be logged as EditEvents, host rosters supplied through ContentProvider are not copied into the document, and a host provider may use Math.random or the network while the lint covers only in-repo model packages; a host-edited document then cannot replay standalone. The 'host inputs' deferral covers what hosts may supply, not the persistence of the bridge M3 builds.
required_change: Every bridge command maps one-to-one to a logged EditEvent; host tables are copied into the document with provenance 'host'; a registered provider is checked by a double-run determinism test, or its outputs are recorded in the document.
evidence: ARCH §11 embedding API and bridge, §14 ContentProvider extension point, §6.5 (3) lint scope, deferrals ('host inputs').

claim: The invariant suite and a whole-model canonical hash run after every batch and every edit
claim_full: §5.3 runs the whole invariant suite "after every batch and every edit" (and §7.1 runs it again as the dry run before each commit); several members are whole-model — "the model hash recomputed equals the recorded one" over the canonical serialisation, id uniqueness and reference integrity, containment 100 %, every gate joined to the plaza, every requested feature present — so generation costs O(batches × model) and every edit O(model); CITY ≤ 300 ms, per-district regeneration ≤ 30 ms, a plot edit ≤ 5 ms and edit-to-redraw < 100 ms are unattainable as written.
required_change: Give every invariant a declared scope (batch-local = the touched faces plus their 1-ring; stage-end; save; CI-only) and check batch-local ones incrementally. Redefine the model hash as a Merkle digest over the plat tree (per-face and per-entity digests → block → district → level → model), updated along dirty paths; keep the canonical serialisation only for golden files and export. Verify per batch only the touched subtree's digest. Add a cost test: per-edit validation time flat from TOWN to METROPOLIS (± 20 %). Decide it before M0's determinism spike, because goldens, K-3 snapshot verification and the locality oracle all compare this hash.
evidence: ARCH §5.3 (title; hash member), §7.1 (dry run), §13.2 ("runs after every batch on B-CITY"), §6.2 (hash over the canonical serialisation: sorted keys, integer coordinates, floats as shortest round-trip strings), §4.1 batch scopes (S8 per district, S10 per block, S11 per plot, edits per event), §12. Executed (bench_state; a schema-shaped model at §12's CITY counts: 22 250 entities, 5 levels × 60 k vertices): one canonical serialisation + hash = 1 163 ms (65 MB of canonical text); METROPOLIS 2 712 ms. CITY has ≈ 7 300 batches (25 districts + ≈ 1 750 blocks + 5 500 plots): even a 10× faster hash costs ≈ 14 min per generation.

claim: The static index rebuilt at every batch commit makes S10 and S11 cost seconds
claim_full: §3.3 rebuilds the static packed spatial index "once per batch commit" while §4.1 declares one batch per block (S10), one per plot or per block (S11) and one per edit; a rebuild is O(level size), so S10/S11 cost O(batches × level) — the engineering judge's ≈ 48 s K-2 hazard returns at a finer grain, and J-7's statement that batching removed it is false for these scopes.
required_change: Rebuild each level's static index once per stage (and after an edit burst goes idle); serve every query inside a stage and every edit from the dynamic per-level index (uniform grid, O(1) insert and delete), merged into the static index at stage end — or partition static indexes per district so a block or plot commit rebuilds only its district's partition (≤ 1 k items ≈ 0.25 ms). State the rule in §3.3, correct J-7, and add a cost-model test on commit count × level size.
evidence: ARCH §2.2 (`index.static: FlatbushIndex /* rebuilt at batch commit */`), §3.3, §4.1 "Transactions", J-7; judge-engineering §0.2 #4 and K-2 (its fix: "flatbush is rebuilt once per stage commit"). Executed (bench_index; our packed Hilbert R-tree, the flatbush construction): 4.9 ms at 17 k items, 12.5 ms at 42 k. Summed as each level grows to its final size: CITY S10 1.9 s (budget 55 ms), S11 13.4 s (budget 25 ms); METROPOLIS S10 12.7 s, S11 85 s. One plot edit (one L3 + one L4 rebuild): 7.3 ms at CITY, 18.8 ms at METROPOLIS (budget 5 ms). S11 per block instead of per plot is still ≈ 4 s.

claim: The CITY per-stage split omits the dominant term of several stages
claim_full: §12's CITY per-stage split omits the dominant term of several stages: S1 prices 2 M fBm evaluations at 30 ms but also floods, routes and contours a raster the plat's margin makes 2.6× larger; S4 omits the lattice construction; S5 omits the stage boundary's cost-distance field; S6 omits the σ ≈ 60 m smoothing of three fields; S10b and S12 omit their sort and face counts. Measured as specified, these stages cost ≈ 0.8 s at CITY against ≈ 0.1 s budgeted (≈ 1.3 s with the margin raster and a Poisson lattice), so the 300 ms p95 fails before any lane is cut.
required_change: Re-budget each stage with its mechanism named: fBm on a coarse grid plus bilinear refinement; priority-flood with a bucket queue on the integer heights; contours extracted lazily per render tile; the 2.5 m refinement as on-demand interpolation; the margin at ≥ 32 m cells; a jittered hexagonal lattice with adjacency by construction (no Poisson, no Lloyd, no Delaunay); one cost-distance field per growth run on the lattice or a ≥ 20 m raster; fields at 16–32 m with an O(N) blur and kernels splatted within their radius; top-k siting over affinity-filtered candidates; open-field strips as render-time segmentation inside FTG-sized field faces; the context vector counted in S10's per-plot rate. Add a site-and-fields spike to M0 next to the fusion gate, starting from §7's numbers.
evidence: ARCH §12 split; §2.3 (rasters 5 / 8 / 10 m; refined to 2.5 m in the built extent); §3.2 and §4.9 (the plat spans frame + 30 % per side); §4.3 (lattice "Poisson-disc, relaxed once"); §3.1 / D-11 (k = 50, all evaluated); §4.4 (stage boundary = level set of a cost-distance field); §4.5 (three fields, Gaussian σ ≈ 60 m). Executed on the capture machine: fBm 27.4 ns per 2-D simplex evaluation; S1 (fBm + priority-flood + D8 + accumulation + 11 contour levels) 126 ms at 625², 333 ms at 1 000² (frame + margin); raster cost-distance field 70 ms at 625²; separable Gaussian σ = 60 m 67 ms per field (3-box blur 6.4 ms); Poisson lattice 310 ms for 25.7 k points; 12 A* queries 16.6 ms on a 46 k-node lattice; naive siting 98 ms per round × 3 rounds; stream keys 73 ms (SCL-12).

claim: The one-click view defeats the laziness the METROPOLIS budget relies on
claim_full: The first-paint plan relies on laziness that the default view defeats: §4.1 makes S10–S14 lazy per district "after the first paint" (city LOD emitted when S9 commits) and §12 says METROPOLIS "relies on lazy per-district derivation of S10–S13 (only visible districts first)"; but the one-click view shows every district, the owner's PLOT MODEL and stage-3 rulings require footprints at city zoom, and §8.5's city band needs district labels (S13) and the hinterland (S12) — so the complete city frame needs S10–S13 for all districts, and the preview at S9 can only show block masses, the "illusion of buildings" the owner ruled out.
required_change: Define the one-click first paint as the complete city LOD (S0–S13 for every district at city-band detail) and budget METROPOLIS for it. Restrict laziness to what the city band does not draw: yard sub-parts, entrances, roof ridges, street names, addresses, crowns. If an S9 preview is kept, specify its drawing (blocks in a distinct preview style) and that the city frame replaces it exactly once, reported. Write the per-district worker merge protocol (J-12) before M2 if METROPOLIS needs it, not "if profiling demands it".
evidence: ARCH §4.1 ("S10–S14 are lazy per district after the first paint"), §8.5 (city band: "blocks as footprint masses … district labels"), §12 (METROPOLIS clause; the per-district worker arenas "if profiling demands it"), J-12; owner PLOT MODEL ("at city zoom the footprints are what shows") and STAGE 3 ("shows at every zoom, including the city view"). §12's CITY split puts S10 + S10b + S11 + S12 + S13 at 110 ms, ≈ 275 ms at METROPOLIS, all of it on the one-click path. Related: LC-2 and FTG-1 (laziness breaks global siting), MFP-1 (city-zoom look).

claim: The undo snapshot ring multiplies the model by eight; the CITY heap is over budget even without it
claim_full: Memory: regenerate-undo keeps "the last k = 8 snapshots" of the materialised document (plats + entities + field rasters); one CITY snapshot is ≈ 80 MB, so the ring alone is ≈ 640 MB against a ≤ 100 MB CITY heap (≈ 1.6 GB against 300 MB at METROPOLIS, enough for an iOS tab kill); if "bounded by size" keeps k ≈ 1, every older undo is "rebuilt by replay" — a full regeneration plus the log. Even without the ring the CITY working set is ≈ 130–150 MB.
required_change: Replace whole-document snapshots with scoped undo records: the inverse event plus the replaced faces and entities of the regenerated scope, O(scope). Keep periodic checkpoints (every K edits, K chosen so replay stays ≤ 100 ms) instead of an 8-deep ring; if snapshots stay, chunk the arenas per district copy-on-write. Compact the entity store: context vectors and provenance as struct-of-arrays columns, `tableVersions` interned per stage run, `venueMix` referenced from the district rather than copied per plot, `deps` as u32 handles. Define what the memory column counts (JS heap + typed arrays + canvas backing stores + WASM memory, both threads) and test it per rung.
evidence: ARCH §7.4 (regenerate row: "the engine keeps the last k = 8 snapshots, bounded by size: older ones are rebuilt by replay"), §2.9 (`snapshot: { plats, entities, fields, modelHash }`), §12 (memory column; "CITY plat ≈ 60 k vertices × 5 levels ≈ 20 MB"). Executed (bench_state): typed arrays for 5 levels × 60 k vertices = 29 MB; the schema-shaped entity table ≈ 2.1 KB per entity (117 MB for 55 625 entities at METROPOLIS; ≈ 47 MB at CITY's 22 250); plus rasters, indices and the display list (≈ 20 MB by §12).

claim: The worker boundary is unspecified, and the typed API clones the model on every call
claim_full: The worker boundary is unspecified and, as typed, expensive: `PlatApi` passes `Document` by value (`generate → Promise<Document>`, `edit(doc, e)`, `render(doc, …)`, `export(doc, …)`) and `DisplayListBuilder.build` returns `Mark[]` objects with `Record` attributes; with generation in a worker, each call structured-clones — the main thread receives a CITY entity table in 162 ms and a 60 k-mark display list in 140 ms — and "transferable buffers" detach the worker's own arrays, which incremental delivery (S1–S9 preview while S10–S13 continue on the same levels) cannot allow.
required_change: Make the API handle-based (`generate → DocHandle`; the document lives in the worker; `edit(handle, e)`; `export(handle, fmt)` returns bytes) and document, per call, what crosses the boundary and whether it is transferred or copied. Make the display list columnar (typed arrays: mark kind, semantic id, entity handle, z, LOD mask, geometry offsets into one Int32 coordinate buffer, attribute columns), delivered as per-group deltas and transferred, never cloned; keep the worker's working buffers (transfer slices). State that SharedArrayBuffer is optional and needs cross-origin isolation from the embedding host. Budget the main thread's receive work per delivery (≤ 4 ms) and test it.
evidence: ARCH §4.1 ("a Web Worker with transferable buffers and incremental delivery" — the only statement on the boundary), §11 embedding API, §14 `PlatApi`, `DisplayListBuilder`, `Mark` (§8.1). Executed (bench_state; v8 serialise / deserialise = the structured-clone algorithm): CITY entity table 19.4 MB, sender 60 ms + receiver 162 ms; display list 60 k marks (17.7 MB, close to §12's ≈ 20 MB): sender 46 ms + main-thread receive 140 ms; 125 k marks: 208 ms; METROPOLIS 150 k marks 302 ms, 312 k marks 895 ms.

claim: Per-district retained tiles break under continuous zoom, and print has no assembly path
claim_full: Canvas2D "retained tiles per district" do not survive continuous zoom: a tile's pixel size grows with zoom² × DPR² (a 10 ha district is ≈ 2 400 px square at the B-ZOOM floor of 1:500, ≈ 4 800 px at DPR 2, 92 MB), beyond per-canvas area caps and tab canvas memory; MFCG's per-group caching works because MFCG has no zoom, and even so its forest canvas reached 6 133 × 5 988 px; a zoom step at METROPOLIS re-rasterises every visible tile (MFCG's full-frame replay: 170–230 ms); §12 drops O12 (b)'s zoom clause and its declared draw-call and upload budgets; a 300 dpi A2 PNG (≈ 35 Mpx) has no assembly path that avoids one giant canvas.
required_change: Replace per-district tiles with a screen-space tile pyramid (256–512 px tiles at √2 zoom steps; a district change invalidates the tiles its bounds intersect — also GEO-28's alternative); an LRU canvas-memory budget in bytes per hardware tier; scaled interim tiles during zoom gestures and progressive re-raster in viewport order in the tile worker. Declare the O12 (b) draw-call and upload budgets and put zoom into §12. For print, render horizontal bands of tiles and stream each band into the PNG encoder, so no canvas exceeds one tile. Count shadow compositing buffers in the budget.
evidence: ARCH §8.5 (tiles per district; OffscreenCanvas; print by tiling "300 dpi A2 without artefacts"), §8.1 (`Mark.group` = district at city LOD), §13.4 (B-ZOOM 1:50 000 → 1:500), §12 ("≥ 60 fps pan"); IMPROVEMENTS O12 (b) (pan **and zoom** at ≥ 60 fps, ≥ 30 fps on a low-end laptop, draw calls and uploads per 1 000 buildings "within declared budgets") and (e) (the references' 8 MP ceiling). `profile-mfcg.md` ST-2 (forest canvas 6 133 × 5 988 px), §7.2 (170–230 ms per frame; 345 944 `lineTo`); `visual-spec.md` §1.1 (fixed 1 500 × 1 100 canvas, per-ward canvases at screen bounds).

claim: Trees generated at render with per-tree Poisson sampling and per-tree crowns cannot meet the 16 ms claim
claim_full: Trees are generated at render and "never stored": positions per green entity by Poisson-disc with k = 50 candidates all evaluated (garden 4–6 m, wood 3–5 m), crowns per tree by the lobed-crown generator; measured at 11–12 µs per tree for positions alone, 10 000 trees cost ≈ 115 ms before any crown is built or drawn, so O19 (e) "≥ 10 000 trees within a 16 ms frame" and §12's 200 k-tree pan hold only if generation is cached off the frame — which the text does not say. D-11 justifies k = 50 as "cheap" at render; it is not.
required_change: Make the tile-stamp path normative for every scatter class (a few precomputed blue-noise tiles per class, built once per session, stamped with a per-entity offset and rotation from its stream, clipped by point-in-polygon), with jittered grids for orchards and avenues. Build a crown library per style (≈ 20 per class) once per session, drawn as sprites in Canvas2D and as instances in WebGL2. Generate instances per tile in the tile worker and cache them by entity for the session, with positions independent of the LOD band (LC-20; the band selects only the crown symbol and a deterministic thinning) — still never persisted. Restate O19 (e) with what the 16 ms covers, a placement budget (≤ 1 µs per tree) and a draw budget.
evidence: ARCH §4.9 (trees-at-render row; O19 (e)), §3.1 Poisson row (both Bridson k = 50 and "a fixed 140-point tile stamped per area" are named, without saying which is normative), D-11, J-10, §8.2 `crown(lobes, jitter)`, §12. Executed (bench_poisson_astar): 11.4–12.1 µs per accepted point; one 36 ha wood = 14 477 trees in 170 ms. References: MFCG tiles one precomputed 140-point pattern (≈ 200 point tests per filled area) and builds 20 crowns once per session (ST-2); NG's crowns have 120–180 vertices from ≈ 20 `bloat` calls per tree, 6 canvas ops per tree (§3.9).

claim: Edits cost what the city costs, not what the scope costs
claim_full: Edits scale with the city, not the scope: §7.3 re-runs "the label and display stages globally" after every regeneration, which at CITY is already S13 10 ms + S14 20 ms = the whole 30 ms per-district budget (≈ 75 ms at METROPOLIS) before any local work; replaying the edit log (load verification "immediately for ≤ CITY", undo beyond the ring, migration) repeats the global stages per edit, O(edits × city); and MFCG's warp tools are a live staged preview, while every PLAT warp event goes through dry run, suite and re-derivation.
required_change: Make S13 and S14 incremental: a regeneration marks a dirty region; S14 re-emits only changed entities' marks and groups; tiles intersecting the region are invalidated; S13 re-places only labels whose candidates intersect it, plus a priority cascade that stops when nothing more moves. Add a replay mode that applies the whole log to the model and runs S13/S14 once at the end, bounded by SCL-5's checkpoints. Add a warp preview mode (vertex moves on L1 and redraw of the affected tiles at ≥ 30 fps; invariants and re-derivation on Apply only). State §12's edit budgets as functions of scope size and test that the same scope costs the same from TOWN to METROPOLIS.
evidence: ARCH §7.3 ("re-run only the label and display stages globally"), §12 (per-district regeneration ≤ 30 ms; single plot edit ≤ 5 ms; edit-to-redraw < 100 ms; S13 10 ms; S14 20 ms), §2.9 (load re-verification), §7.4 (undo "rebuilt by replay"), §7.5, §7.1 (warp event with dry-run validation), §3.4 `warp`. `mfcg-posts-a.md` §T4 (warp is "a staged, committable edit … Apply and Discard"). Arithmetic: 300 edits × ≥ 30 ms of global stages ≈ 9 s of replay at CITY.

claim: Label placement is priced for district spines but specified for every label at every LOD
claim_full: Label placement is priced at 10 ms for district spines, but the specified work is the full map at every LOD band in the model: district and water spines, street labels "repeated per segment", addresses along every way (one per building), point labels, each fitted and checked in a screen-space collision index per LOD with protected obstacles and "0 collisions at every LOD" as an invariant; screen-space collisions also change with zoom inside a band, so the result is either wrong between band stops or recomputed per zoom on the main thread, unbudgeted — GEO-29's option (b) turns it into exactly that runtime cost.
required_change: Split S13 into model-side candidate generation (spines, anchors, alternates, priorities, widths from bundled font metrics per GEO-29 (a)) and view-side selection (greedy by priority in a viewport-culled grid index, per zoom stop, in the tile worker) with a budget (≤ 2 ms per zoom stop for ≤ 2 000 visible candidates). Place addresses and street names only for visible tiles at their LOD. Check "0 collisions" at declared zoom stops. State S13's model budget at METROPOLIS.
evidence: ARCH §9 (area, path and point labels, addresses, per-LOD screen-space `rbush`, protected features, 0 collisions), §12 (S13 10 ms, "spines cached per district"), §7.3 (global re-run), §8.5 (continuous zoom with hysteresis); GEO-29. MFCG places ≈ 60–190 letters per city along ≈ 15 skeleton ridges (`profile-mfcg.md` §6.2, §8), and its label text costs 40–73 ms per frame (§7.2). METROPOLIS carries 12–15 k buildings, hence 12–15 k address candidates.

claim: The document persists derivable rasters and five copies of shared boundaries
claim_full: The `.plat` snapshot persists derivable, poorly-compressible data: the prosperity and density rasters (Float32 at terrain resolution gzip to 2.7 MB at CITY's 625², 7.0 MB over the plat's margin, 11.4 MB at METROPOLIS) against document budgets of ≤ 3 MB and ≤ 8 MB; five separate per-level DCELs store every inherited boundary up to four times; `report.streamKeysUsed` holds ≈ 10⁵ strings. FTG's 593 KB for 2 798 buildings, population and trees is the stated bar.
required_change: Do not persist derivable fields: persist brush strokes and recompute on load with SCL-3's O(N) blur, or store a quantised coarse cache (Uint8 at 32 m ≈ 40 KB at CITY). Persist geometry once — a shared vertex store with level-tagged edges (GEO-1's alternative) or L3/L4 only, with L0–L2 re-derived from the recipe. Record stream keys only for attempts > 0 and ladder uses. Add a document-size test per rung against §12 and against FTG's bytes per building.
evidence: ARCH §2.9 (`snapshot.fields: { prosperity: Raster; density: Raster }`; "FTG's economy … is the bar"), §5.4 (`streamKeysUsed: string[]`), §2.2 (levels are separate DCELs), §12 (document gz ≤ 0.6 / 3 / 8 MB); `ftg-payload-visual.md` §1 (593 KB). Executed (bench_siting_doc): one Float32 field 1.36 MB gz at 625², 3.49 MB at 1 000², 5.72 MB at 1 280²; entity JSON for 22 250 schema-shaped records 1.25 MB gz; 10⁵ stream keys 0.50 MB gz. Geometry for 5 × 60 k vertices ≈ 2–3 MB gz (PLAUSIBLE). CITY total ≈ 6.5–7.5 MB.

claim: String-path stream keys cost a third of the CITY budget, and the encoding is frozen after M1
claim_full: Every stream key is derived by building a UTF-8 path string and hashing it (§6.1); measured at 0.73 µs per key, the design's own ≈ 10⁵ keys at CITY cost ≈ 73 ms (≈ 30 % of the 240 ms p50) and ≈ 2.5 × 10⁵ at METROPOLIS ≈ 195 ms, none of it budgeted; because the key encoding fixes every seed's output (D-15: reversal cost "high after M1"), a later speed fix would shift every golden.
required_change: Derive keys from structured components, not strings: stage id (u16), the entity's canonical-id hash (computed once when the id is minted and cached in the arena), concern id from the registry (u16), attempt and epoch, mixed by the 32-bit-lane mixer into 128 bits; keep the textual path for reports only; budget ≤ 0.1 µs per key; decide it in the M0 determinism spike, before any golden is signed.
evidence: ARCH §6.1 (canonical UTF-8 path; two 32-bit-lane mixers; "≈ 10⁵ keys" in a B-CITY city; streams created on demand, including `style/*` and `render.trees` at render time), D-15, §12. Executed (bench_state): 10⁵ path strings → 128-bit keys (TextEncoder + four murmur-style lanes) in 73 ms; 2.5 × 10⁵ in 195 ms.

claim: The stage-3 hook has no cost contract, and laziness cannot apply at the city view
claim_full: The stage-3 hook has no cost contract: compositions are "lazily generated", yet the owner requires the composed footprints "at every zoom, including the city view" and O17 (i) requires the same footprint hash at every LOD, so every building must be composed before the first city frame; at Fantasy Manor's measured 0.6–1.7 ms per building model, METROPOLIS's 12–15 k buildings take ≈ 7–25 s.
required_change: Split the interface into `outline(input) → footprint rings + heights` (cheap and deterministic, used at every LOD and in exports; ≤ 20 µs per building) and `compose(input, lod)` for wings, roofs and rooms, computed lazily per visible tile. Require the outline to equal the union of the composed wings (a contract test) so O17 (i) holds. Put a per-building cost budget and a METROPOLIS total into the hook's documentation; the stage-3 intake measures FM-class composition time per building class.
evidence: ARCH §2.6 (`composition?: Composition /* stage 3: lazily generated */`; `BuildingGenerator.compose(…, lod)`), §8.6, §15.2 O17 (i); owner STAGE 3 ruling; §12 (METROPOLIS 12 000–15 000 buildings, 700 ms p50). `captures/manor/README.md` cost table: `Manor.new` 1.7 / 0.8 / 0.6 ms in gens 0–2 (model only; its view and shadow cost more).

claim: The layered SVG export has no LOD rule and no size budget
claim_full: The layered SVG export emits one element per entity with its id, trees as `<use>`, hatching as paths and per-glyph text, at an unstated LOD; at METROPOLIS that is ≈ 15 k footprints × 2 marks, ≈ 30 k yard parts, the ways, and up to ≈ 200 k tree instances at district LOD — ≈ 20–35 MB and 100–300 k elements, against MFCG's 6.3 MB and ≈ 35 k paths for 15 392 buildings — so O11 (h) "opens in Inkscape / Illustrator with layers intact" is not credible at that size.
required_change: Specify the export LOD (city band by default; district band on request, with a size warning). Emit compound paths per (semantic, district) with an id side table (a data attribute on each group plus a JSON map from subpath ranges to entity ids) instead of one element per entity. Emit trees as one compound path per green entity or per tile, and per-glyph text only for curved labels. Add an export size and element-count test at METROPOLIS (for example ≤ 1.5× MFCG's bytes per building, ≤ 60 000 elements) and an open-time check in Inkscape to O11 (h).
evidence: ARCH §11 SVG row (entity ids on elements; instances as `<use>`; hatching as paths), §8.7, §15.2 O11 (h), O12 (c); §12 (200 k trees at METROPOLIS). `captures/mfcg/exports-2026-09-25/README.md` (size 80: 15 392 buildings, SVG 6 297 685 bytes, 15 367 roof paths + 19 526 dark footprints; size 40: 0.42–0.66 MB). Our size is PLAUSIBLE arithmetic at ≈ 70–150 bytes per element.

claim: Proxy thumbnails lost their "at town size"
claim_full: §7.8 promises six S0–S4 proxy thumbnails "within 1 s for all six" for the size and water controls, dropping IMPROVEMENTS O16 (e)'s "at town size"; S1 alone measures 126 ms at CITY and 267 ms at METROPOLIS, so six proxies take ≈ 0.8–1.6 s before S4.

claim: First-map targets disagree, and METROPOLIS's depends on an optional backend without text
claim_full: The first-map targets disagree and METROPOLIS's rests on an optional backend without text: §1.2 and O12 (g) say under 1 s, §12 says ≤ 2 s for METROPOLIS, and METROPOLIS's first frame "≤ 1 s (progressive; WebGL2 tier)" depends on WebGL2, which §1.7 makes optional and whose SDF text is deferred.

evidence: ARCH §1.2, §1.7 (WebGL2 optional), §12 (time to first map ≤ 2 s METROPOLIS; first frame "WebGL2 tier"), §15.2 O12 (g), Deferrals ("WebGL2 SDF text").

claim: The test plan has no compute budget
claim_full: The CI plan has no compute budget: B-CITY's 12 000 generations with the suite after every batch, B-EDIT's 10⁵ sequences each checked against a from-scratch regeneration, B-FUZZ's 10⁶ inputs per primitive and nightly five-engine goldens with a PNG per LOD and preset add up to ≈ 10–20 CPU-hours per full run, so the suite cannot gate changes.
required_change: Tier CI with stated wall-clock budgets: a PR tier of minutes (for example 50 seeds per rung, 10⁴ fuzz cases per primitive, 10³ edit sequences) and a nightly full tier; sample the oracle per sequence, not per edit.
evidence: ARCH §13.1–§13.3, §16 M3 exit (10⁵ sequences), §7.3 (oracle). Arithmetic: 12 000 × ≈ 0.47 s (TOWN 0.1, CITY 0.3, METROPOLIS 1 s) ≈ 1.6 CPU-h before the suite; 10⁵ oracle regenerations × ≈ 0.3 s ≈ 8 CPU-h; 10⁶ × ≈ 20 primitives × 50 µs–1 ms ≈ 0.3–5.5 CPU-h. claim: Cost-model tests cannot see the super-linear mechanisms that matter
claim_full: The cost-model tests fit each stage's time against its entity count "across the rungs" — three points — and time only generation, so they cannot catch the mechanisms that actually go super-linear here (per-batch work that grows with batches × level size; per-edit work that grows with city size).
required_change: Sweep ≥ 6 sizes per stage and fail on a log-log slope above ≈ 1.15; add per-edit cost-versus-model-size tests (edit cost must be flat across rungs for a fixed scope).
evidence: ARCH §13.2; SCL-1, SCL-2, SCL-9.

claim: Evolution state has no compaction rule
claim_full: Evolution state grows without a compaction rule: every entity carries its whole lifecycle history, JOINed plots keep their members, superseded entities keep `supersedes` links, and epochs append; a 20-epoch town's working set and document grow with its churn, and nothing bounds them.
required_change: Keep lifecycle history in an append-only event block keyed by id rather than inside each entity; move demolished and superseded entities to an archive block excluded from the working set and indexes; state a per-epoch growth budget and test a 20-epoch town's heap and document size.
evidence: ARCH §2.1 (JOIN members kept as history; `supersedes`), §2.8 (`Lifecycle.history` inside each entity), §4.11, §2.9 (`epochs: EpochRecord[]`); owner EVOLUTION ruling.

claim: The per-generation statistics record is unbudgeted and partly uncomputable in the model
claim_full: A statistics record is emitted by every generation, including metrics that need all-pairs routing (detour index), neighbour graphs (Moran's I), KS tests and tree pair-correlation — the last over trees that exist only at render — and §12 has no stage or budget for it.
required_change: Split the record into an O(n) core emitted per generation (counts, sums, histograms) with a budget, and the expensive metrics computed on demand or in the bench only; compute tree statistics from the tile-stamped scatter in the bench.
evidence: ARCH §13.2 ("The statistics record emitted per generation"), §15.2 O6 (d) ("100 % of generations emit a statistics record"), O4 (b), O18 (b), O19 (d), §4.9 (trees never stored), §12.

claim: The pure-JS boolean fallback is budgeted nowhere
claim_full: §12's budgets assume Clipper2 in WebAssembly, but the pure-JS fallback ships too and hosts whose content-security policy forbids WebAssembly compilation get it; its cost on S9's per-district unions and the concave insets is budgeted nowhere.
required_change: Have the M0 benchmark time both engines on S9 and S11 workloads; give §12 a fallback budget or make WebAssembly a stated requirement of the embed contract; record in the generation report which engine ran.

claim: The `ink` preset is written in MFCG's unit, and nothing maps PLAT's realistic model to drawn symbols
claim_full: The `ink` preset is written in MFCG's internal unit ("wall 1.9 u", "offset ≈ (+0.25, +0.7) u"), which PLAT does not have (read as metres, the numbers are a quarter of MFCG's drawn sizes), and there is no symbolisation law from PLAT's realistic model to drawn symbols. Drawn at model width, the 2–3 m wall band is a third of MFCG's weight (1.6–2.4 px against 6.2 px at MFCG's size-40 view scale; 0.56 px against 1.7 px at its size-80 scale, under the 2-px floor) and towers and gate blocks have no size; drawn at MFCG's 7.6 m over a 2.5 m band, the symbol overhangs an unspecified setback onto plots. At CITY and METROPOLIS frame zoom 0.5-px paper hairlines take ≈ 39 % and ≈ 58 % of a 10.3 m house's pixels — MFCG's own size-80 "outlines swamp" weakness — and the 1.4-px METROPOLIS house breaks O12 (a)'s floor with no rule for meeting it.
required_change: Add a symbolisation table to every style sheet: per semantic and LOD band, drawn width = clamp(k × model width, minPx, maxPx) or a fixed paper width, units explicit (m or paper px), no "u"; calibrate the ink rows on the MFCG export at matched view scale (wall ≈ 7.6 m-equivalent, tower diameter ≈ 2 × drawn wall, gate = gap + two blocks ≈ 2 × wall width, road core 8 m, pier 4.8 m); exaggeration never enters the model, GeoJSON or VTT; exaggerated walls draw after footprints and the setback band covers half the overhang (or the symbol is clipped); outlines thin then drop by band (an ink "thin lines" row at city LOD); sub-floor footprints go through MFP-1's footprint-mass generalisation; census: drawn wall, tower and road px within ± 15 % of MFCG's at the matched scale, outline share of footprint pixels at city LOD ≤ 25 %.
evidence: ARCH §8.2 l. 1354 (ink in u), §2.1 and §1.7 data row (every length carries a unit), §4.8 l. 903 (wall 2–3 m), §2.7 `Tower.radiusCm` (no rule), §8.5 l. 1390–1391 (min symbol ≥ 2 px), O12 (a) l. 1879. MFCG export `values`: roadWidth 8, wallThickness 7.6, towerRadius 7.6, planks 4.8 (exports README; metres per redteam-mfcg EXP, 1 u = 4.00 m); SVG `scale(3.263)` for gates4; profile-mfcg EG-4 (wall ≈ 5–6 px, gate = gap + two ≈ 12 × 13 px blocks), §10.3 (outlines in screen px, widths in world units); visual-spec §0.2, §1.3 step 10 (walls after buildings); IMPROVEMENTS O12 answers (size 80: outlines swamp, buildings "read as texture"), O6 restraint (symbol scaling in rendering, never in the model); coverage K04 judged "1.9 u" COVERED, K14 Thin lines.

claim: Roles and the contrast test cannot separate gardens from buildings, trees from water, or yards from streets
claim_full: The colour roles and the contrast test cannot keep gardens apart from buildings, trees apart from water, or yards apart from streets. §4.9 puts garden parts on most plots, and the `ink` row allows "four inks on buff paper"; with MFCG-family role values the garden fill is ΔE 0.8 from the building fill, so every planted yard reads as a building filling its plot — the "illusion of buildings" returns through greenery — and woods take the water colour (ΔE 0). The only colour constraint tests luminance between ground, road, building and water, so it passes both collapses and misses hue-separated pairs.
required_change: Add roles `ground` (yard, settled ground), `garden`, `court`, `field`, `verge` (MFP-1 asks for `ground`) with our own ink values; replace the luminance rule by a pairwise matrix with ΔE and ΔL* floors on the pairs that must separate at city zoom (street vs ground, garden vs building, building vs ground, tree vs water, green vs road, wall vs water), checked on rendered city-LOD images in B-ZOOM and on 100 % of random styles; keep the ink family to ≤ 6–8 visible tones without saturated hues (O12 restraint) so the matrix is met by value steps; record MFCG's green = building and tree = water collapses as reference weaknesses not to copy.
evidence: ARCH §8.2 l. 1341–1342 (roles: no ground, yard, garden, court, field or verge), l. 1360 and O12 (f) (luminance, four classes), §4.9 l. 946 (yard planting by class), l. 962 (restraint). MFCG default `colorGreen` `#A59F93` vs `colorRoof` `#A5A095`, `colorTree` = `colorWater` `#7F7A71` (profile-mfcg §10.1; ST-2: forest "the same grey as water"); EXP ΔE 0.8 and 0.0. MFCG's Complex mode (buildings smaller than lots, ST-7): EXP paper share 0.246 → 0.311 on the same city, streets merge with gaps (047 vs 049 crop); default is Lots (ST-0). FTG: paving `#C6C2BB` with a 1-px rim, settled ground `#BCB8B2`, in-town lawn `#ADB69D` (ftg-payload-visual §8.1, visual-spec §4.3; EXP ΔE 3.7 and 12.4; 002 overview: suburb streets pale through green). NG: street stripe ΔE 14.0 from paper, green courts ΔE 11.9 at ΔL* 1.5 (visual-spec §3.2–§3.6).

claim: The city LOD drops every way below tier 2, so the suburb's streets and the extramural lanes vanish
claim_full: The city LOD draws only tier-1/2 ways, so the suburb regime's offshoot lanes and cul-de-sacs, the gapped rings' rear lanes and the farmsteads' tracks vanish outside the walls, where no continuous building line makes them read as gaps: the plots the suburb lays "directly along the offshoots" float in paper with no street network at the zoom the owner compares. FTG draws its suburb streets as filled corridors at overview zoom; MFCG avoids the case because its extramural houses sit on drawn roads.
required_change: Select city-LOD ways by legibility need, not class: every way that is the only access of a plot not fronting a drawn way (suburb offshoots, ribbon back lanes, farm tracks, extramural lanes) is drawn at city LOD with a lane symbol; intramural lanes stay gaps only where a continuous frontage bounds them (MFP-1); B-ZOOM metric: plots at city LOD whose access way is drawn or bounded by continuous frontage ≥ 95 %; include the suburb in the M1 / M2 side-by-sides against FTG's overview.
evidence: ARCH §8.5 l. 1386–1388 (city band: tier-1/2 ways; intramural alleys as gaps), §4.9 l. 949 (tier 1 = through, primary), §4.4 l. 742 (rear lanes), l. 744 (suburb offshoots as `cul_de_sac` / `lane`, density gaps), §4.9 (farmstead `track`). FTG 002-overview and 001 crops (Greenwood's streets visible at overview zoom); visual-spec §4.4 (filled corridors); profile-mfcg ST-4 (sprawl alleys drawn only with the off-by-default alleys layer, ST-0); redteam-mfcg MFP-6 (suburb regime by default; 50–65 % of a TOWN outside the wall) and EXP ribbon distances (71–85 % within 100 m of a gate road).

claim: District labels cannot fit PLAT's districts at CITY zoom under "≥ 99 % inside" and the protected features
claim_full: District labels cannot fit inside PLAT's 5–15 ha districts at CITY frame zoom under the ≥ 99 %-inside and protected-feature rules: a 10 ha district is ≈ 69 px across at 4.55 m/px, so a 12-glyph letter-spaced name fits only at ≈ 5–6 px (cap ≈ 4 px), and the F-LABEL ladder sends most names to the legend; METROPOLIS is worse. MFCG keeps its curved labels legible at size 80 with districts of median 29 ha and by letting labels overflow; the "minimum size" F-LABEL tests against is unstated.
required_change: State the label legibility floor in px (e.g. cap height ≥ 7 px at 1×) and make the ladder respect it before the legend rung; at city LOD label quarters (adjacent districts of one kind merged until the spine fits the floor, named by the grammar) or allow a declared overflow (≤ 20 % of glyph area outside the face, never over a protected feature or another label); acceptance per rung at the default view: ≥ 12 on-map area labels at or above the floor (MFCG size 80 draws 17), 0 protected overlaps, legend fallbacks reported; measured with the bundled font in B-ZOOM.
evidence: ARCH §9 l. 1419–1431 (size ∝ √area within a band, inside ≥ 99 %, protected features), §5.2 F-LABEL l. 1047 ("the minimum size", no value), §13.5 labels row l. 1629, D-19 (district band 5–15 ha); profile-mfcg §8, visual-spec §1.7 (27 px caps, glyph canvases 15–55 px, size ∝ district); coverage-audit-mfcg J02 (2019 labels overflowed their areas), J05 (skeleton labels, small fitted curves); redteam-mfcg EXP district areas (size 80: 17 districts, median 29 ha) and MFP-10 (36–70 labels at MFCG-80 scale); GEO-29 (label fit depends on the text engine).

claim: Decoration is keyed by LOD band, so trees and roof detail re-roll at every band switch
claim_full: Decoration is keyed "by entity id and LOD band" (§6.1), so tree positions and shapes, scatter, roof detail and hatch phase are re-drawn from a new stream at every band switch: zooming a leafy district from city to neighbourhood makes every tree jump at the district and neighbourhood thresholds (and again on each hysteresis reversal), against O12 (a) and §8.5's "no feature pops more than once". §13.4 tests only the footprint hash. PLAT would re-roll positions as well as shapes — worse than MFCG, whose re-picked crowns are a recorded defect.
required_change: Key decoration by entity id and instance index only, never by band; generate each green entity's instances once at the finest spacing with a stable per-instance rank and let coarser bands draw a deterministic subset (rank ≤ k) or an aggregate fill; crown shape, colour jitter and hatch phase keyed by instance or entity id; evaluate forest edges once in world units; extend B-ZOOM so every decoration instance appears at most once across a city → neighbourhood → city sweep and keeps its position once visible, and an unchanged view re-renders pixel-identically.
evidence: ARCH §6.1 l. 1103, §4.9 l. 955 (instances at render from `treeStream`), l. 962 (area fill → crowns → lobed trees by LOD), §8.5 l. 1391, §13.4 l. 1598–1603, O12 (a); profile-mfcg ST-2 (tree positions are model data; crowns re-picked from an un-reset stream on every render, visibly), ST-12 ("make the pick deterministic if re-renders must match; MFCG's does not"); coverage-audit-ng-shared XB32 (tree instances have no export path).

claim: Per-district tiles "re-rasterised only when marks change" cannot follow continuous zoom
claim_full: Canvas2D tiles "re-rasterised only when a district's marks change" cannot follow continuous zoom: paper-unit hairlines and casings change world size at every zoom step, so a cached tile is either bitmap-scaled (hairlines blur to ≈ 1 px or thin to ≈ 0.25 px, casing Δ = 2h lost, screen-space labels no longer match) or every visible district is re-rasterised per step (at MFCG's recorded 170–230 ms per redraw of ≈ 15 k buildings, i.e. 11–15 µs per building, ≈ 50–90 ms for a CITY view and ≈ 130–225 ms for METROPOLIS: 4–20 fps against O12 (b)'s "pan and zoom at ≥ 60 fps"). §12 quietly states "≥ 60 fps pan". MFCG's per-ward cache is why MFCG has no zoom.
required_change: A tile pyramid keyed (district, band, zoom level) at ≤ √2 steps with per-level re-raster budgets (ms per 1 000 buildings) measured at M1; bitmap scaling only transiently within one level during a gesture, re-raster in the worker (OffscreenCanvas) and swap; tile margins ≥ the largest cross-tile effect (shadow length, crown radius, casing width) and one global casing-before-body order (GEO-28); separate zoom fps from pan fps in §12 and B-ZOOM; a hairline-fidelity check at every settled zoom (casing Δ = 2h ± 0.1 px, hairline ≈ 50 % ink).
evidence: ARCH §8.5 l. 1390–1398, §8.2 (paper-unit hairlines), §12 l. 1549 ("≥ 60 fps pan") and its MFCG bar (170–230 ms Canvas replay), O12 (b) (IMPROVEMENTS: "Pan and zoom at ≥ 60 fps"); visual-spec §1.1 (one bitmap per ward), §6 item 3 ("sub-pixel widths matter: MFCG's 0.119 px hairline is the look"); IMPROVEMENTS O12 answers (MFCG: no zoom for "technical reasons"; NG rasterises in 73–111 ms); GEO-28 (per-district tiles break the casing order at seams).

claim: The `lit` preset cannot be built as specified on either backend, and its assets have no budget
claim_full: The `lit` preset (D-1's second preset; M2's side-by-side against FTG) is specified as programs the default Canvas2D backend cannot run — normal-mapped canopy and stone shading, and "soft" shadows that need the bitmap filters §8.4 says the design avoids — and a WebGL2 tier that must stay within a pixel threshold of Canvas2D, which caps the lit look at a tonal split. The same WebGL2 tier carries the METROPOLIS first frame but specifies no stroke tessellation for MFCG's round-joined sub-pixel hairlines. PLAT's own texture set (FTG's is creative content) has no list, format or budget.
required_change: Declare a reference backend per preset (ink → Canvas2D, lit → WebGL2) and scope the cross-backend pixel test to one preset with a declared degradation list (lit on Canvas2D: hard offset shadows, two-tone faces, no normal maps); specify the WebGL2 pipeline both uses need: stroke tessellation with round joins and caps and coverage-correct sub-pixel widths (the ink census must pass on WebGL2), per-face roof normals from the skeleton, normal-mapped canopy and stone shading with one directional light, soft shadows as a per-tile shadow mask blurred once (or alpha-mask quads), water depth and foam from a shoreline distance field; add `penumbraPx` to `shadowPass`; list PLAT's own texture set with provenance, resolution and tiling and cost it in M2; add the crop attribute VS27 asks for.
evidence: ARCH §8.2 l. 1339 ("WebGL2 with a Canvas2D tonal-split approximation"), l. 1355 (lit: soft drop shadows, depth ramp, foam), §8.4 l. 1379–1381 (FM's cost "avoided by vector offsets, not bitmap filters"), §8.5 l. 1396 (WebGL2: hatch, crowns, SDF text later, pixel test against Canvas2D), O12 (c), §12 METROPOLIS row (WebGL2 tier), §16 M2 l. 1919, §17 (no reference textures), D-1. visual-spec §4.1–§4.4 (three.js, per-vertex colour, normals, `sphere_normal`, `tall_stone_normal`, `circle_alpha`, `edges_alpha`, directional light); ftg-posts-c §2.13 (depth and foam as distance-from-shore functions in the water shader); manor.md (FM's soft shadow = 11–15 bitmap passes, ≈ 90 % of render); coverage-audit-ftg K04 (soft shadows judged COVERED), K07; coverage-audit-ng-shared VS27 (no crop attribute).

claim: Plot boundaries have no walls, fences, hedges or gates
claim_full: Plot boundaries carry no walls, fences, hedges or gates: the edge types are `plot_line`, `party_wall` and `invisible`, yards are areas, and the compound's "gate on the access edge" has no geometry. At district LOD every detached, compound, hovel, vacant or garden frontage is an open yard edge — once MFP-1 tones yards, the street edge there is a tone step only; a compound's court cannot be told from a public square or the neighbour's yard; NG's walled manor compounds cannot be drawn; VTT scenes lack every yard wall. FTG shows the symbology risk: its fenced yards "read as broken buildings".
required_change: Add a boundary treatment to plot edges (frontage, side, rear) — none, fence, hedge, wall or railing, with gate openings on access edges — chosen by the site-plan table by class, prosperity band and arrangement (calibratable data rows); draw it at district LOD as a stroke distinct from buildings (never filled, weight ≤ ½ the building outline, gaps at gates); count walled or fenced frontage toward O17 (d) streetwall continuity; export walls and fences to VTT and GeoJSON; NG's manor wall uses the same field.
evidence: ARCH §2.4 l. 359, §2.5 l. 375 (yard parts), §4.7 S11 l. 882–889 (arrangements; "a gate on the access edge"), §8.5 district band, §11 VTT row, O17 (d); profile-neighbourhood §3.8 (manor groves fill "its entire walled plot"); coverage-audit-ng-shared N27 (manor enclosure wall not modelled; L, stage 2); coverage-audit-ftg D06 (FTG walls and fences drawn with road controls); IMPROVEMENTS O12 answers (FTG: "fenced yards read as broken buildings"); coverage-audit-vg VN-154 (VG fences and hedges between plots); NG crop (continuous rows around green courts keep the street edge).

claim: The style families are not defined across the four LOD bands
claim_full: The style families are not defined across the four LOD bands: `ink` covers city and district items, `hatched` is "the stage-2 close-up tier", and §8.5 defines the neighbourhood band in NG's own terms. A default-ink user who opens a district gets either the ink city drawing magnified — MFCG's District View weakness ("drawn exactly in the same way … often looks disjointed") — or a switch to `hatched`, where the palette and line idiom jump from grey print to brown hatched roofs at one threshold, contradicting PART II's "a closer level of detail of the same picture". `lit` has no close-up band either.
required_change: Every shipped family defines all four bands with invariant colour roles — detail is added, roles are never remapped: `ink` at neighbourhood LOD = an ink-family close-up (MFCG's Hip/Gable ridge hairlines, NG-style tapered ticks in the ink role on the roof colour, prism shadows at an ink alpha, cobbles as ink stipple); `hatched` and `lit` define their city bands too; additive detail cross-faded over the hysteresis interval; B-ZOOM role-continuity check (mean roof and ground colour ΔE < 2 across each band switch in a family); the stage-2 side-by-side against NG uses `hatched` with an ink close-up alongside.
evidence: ARCH §8.2 l. 1354–1356, §8.5 l. 1386–1389 (neighbourhood band = NG-class content), §8.6 l. 1402 and II.4 l. 2059 ("the hatched preset at neighbourhood LOD"), §14 `StyleSheet` (per-band order, programs, budgets), PART II l. 1992; IMPROVEMENTS O12 answers (MFCG District View, 101942512); visual-spec §1.4 vs §3.4 (flat grey roofs vs two-tone brown roofs with ink ticks); profile-mfcg ST-3 (MFCG's own close-up: per-footprint ridge hairlines on flat roofs).

claim: Single-wing L/T footprints and model-fixed roof kinds cannot produce NG's per-wing "fake" gables
claim_full: Single-wing L/T footprints and model-fixed roof kinds cannot produce NG's per-wing "fake" gables, its two-tone law or its hatching. NG draws every wing as a rectangle with a ridge on its long axis, cuts the roof into two slopes along it and hatches across each slope; PLAT stores an L/T as "a single-wing composition" with one `ridgeAxis`, so the hatched preset either splits an L by one ridge line (the cross arm gets a lengthwise split and hatching) or draws a hip-and-valley skeleton NG never draws, with no rule for which faces are lit. Roof construction follows the model's `roof.kind`, so changing preset cannot change it; the derived-roof cache has no construction key.
required_change: Store wings in the base: every non-rectangular outline-builder footprint is a set of rectangular wings (L = 2, T = 2–3), each with ridge axis, heights and roof kind, the footprint their union (footprint hash unchanged at city LOD); make roof construction a style-sheet parameter (plain, skeleton-hip, skeleton-gable, fake-gable-per-wing) over the stored wings, with the derived-roof cache keyed by (entity, construction); define two-tone assignment for any face set (lit when the face normal faces the light, NG's multiplier otherwise); census: roofs per wing, hatch triangles per wing 15–20, no ridge stroke, footprint-only outline (N35).
evidence: ARCH §2.6 l. 419–423 (L/T "single-wing composition", one `roof` per building), §4.7 l. 893–894 (roof kind by class: skeleton hip or gable), §8.5 l. 1398 (derived roofs cached by entity id), §8.2 l. 1356 (`roof`, `hatch(ridge)`); profile-neighbourhood §3.5 (Building 779 ≈ Wing 787, `Rect.ofPoly` = OBB, `getRidge`, `swapAxes` ≈ 36 %), §3.6 (`hatchRoof` = cut by the ridge, ≈ 8.5 chords × 2 triangles; dark = lit × lerp(ambience, shadow, 0.4)), BG-3 (no ridge stroked); watabou-extra-b T5 ("fake" gables preferred by eye; a style parameter, not correctness), T4; profile-mfcg ST-3 (per-footprint skeleton; gable via `addGables`; failure → plain); coverage-audit-ng-shared N28, N29, N35.

claim: The roof downgrade "hip-from-OBB" is itself a visual surprise
claim_full: The F-SKELETON roof downgrade "hip-from-OBB" draws hip lines from OBB corners that lie outside a non-rectangular footprint and cross its edges — a visual surprise the ladder claims to exclude; MFCG draws a roof whose gable pass fails plain.
required_change: Downgrade roofs to plain (no ridge lines), or clip the OBB hip to the footprint and drop sub-pixel lines; a ladder-coverage fixture renders the downgrade and asserts no roof line outside its footprint.
evidence: ARCH §5.2 F-SKELETON l. 1046, §5.1 tier 4, §13.1 l. 1575 ("never a crash and never a visual surprise"); profile-mfcg ST-3, ST-12 ("drawn plain, not hipped").

claim: The display list has no raster mark
claim_full: The display list has no raster mark, so the base should-have relief tier (hillshade), terrain colour ramps and distance-field water effects have nowhere to live: `MarkKind` and `GeomRef` cover faces, chains, point sets and text spines only. VN-031 asks for a hillshade program; a program still needs a raster geometry to run on.
required_change: Add a `field` mark kind with a raster `GeomRef` (world-space grid, resolution per band, value → colour ramp or light) so hillshade, FTG's depth ramp and VG's beach band are data; zero cost when unused.
evidence: ARCH §8.1 (`MarkKind`, `GeomRef`), §2.3 (terrain is a raster outside the plat), §15.2 "O12 extras (relief tiers …)" → §8.5 (no mechanism); coverage-audit-vg VN-031 (hillshade MISSING, medium), VN-029 (relief marks PARTIAL), §5 conflict note; visual-spec §2.3, §7 item 4 (VG beach band from a raster pass); ftg-posts-c §2.13 (FTG depth and foam as distance fields).

claim: Shore treatments need per-segment shore marks
claim_full: Shore treatments vary per shore segment in the references — FTG's foam on the open sea, weaker on rivers, none in the sheltered harbour; beach, pebble and cliff strips — but the display list strokes the water face's outline uniformly, so foam lands on quays and inside the harbour basin and cliffs are painted as beach, although the model already types `bankKinds` per shore segment.
required_change: S14 emits shore chains per bank segment with `bankKind`, `waterKind` and `exposure` attributes; foam, beach, cliff and quay programs select on them; census: foam on 0 % of quay and harbour segments.
evidence: ARCH §2.3 (`bankKinds` per shore segment), §4.2 S1 (7), §8.2 `bands(...)` over the face, l. 1355 (lit: "water depth ramp and foam line"); ftg-posts-c §2.13 (ocean foam, weaker river foam, heuristic ocean vs river); ftg-payload-visual §8.1–§8.2 (harbour a distinct tone; foam exactly on the waterline; beach strip); visual-spec §4.2 (`pebble_beach`, `cliff`), §4.4.

claim: Avenue crowns cover the tier-1 casings at city zoom
claim_full: Avenue trees along tier-1 ways cover the casings of the town's most important streets at city zoom: the avenue rule plants crowns 8–12 m apart on both sides of through and primary ways, trees draw after roads, and the city-LOD restraint (area fill → crowns → lobed trees) says nothing about line greenery — 6–10 m crowns are 1.5–2 px blobs on each kerb at 4.55 m/px.
required_change: At city LOD draw avenues as a thin green edge line inside the corridor, or not at all, never as crowns over a casing; B-ZOOM check: no tree mark covers a tier-1/2 casing at city LOD.
evidence: ARCH §4.9 l. 949 (avenues), l. 955 (crown diameters "consistent with building sizes"), l. 962 (restraint); profile-mfcg ST-2 (trees after wards and fields, before walls; never on roads in the screenshots), coverage-audit-mfcg K16.

claim: A paper-role halo misfires once blocks have a ground tone
claim_full: The label halo is the paper role; once MFP-1 gives blocks a ground tone, and over water, forest or fields, a paper halo prints light blotches around every glyph. MFCG's paper halo works only because its paper is also its road and ground.
required_change: Halo role = the local background role under the glyph (sampled along the spine), or a knock-out that restores the underlying fills; checked with VIS-2's contrast matrix.
evidence: ARCH §9 l. 1422 ("halo in the paper role"), §8.2 `halo(text, paper, px)`; visual-spec §1.2 (paper = road = ground in MFCG), §1.7 (≈ 2 px paper halo), §4.5 (FTG cream halo plus drop shadow); redteam-mfcg MFP-1 (a) (ground role).

claim: "Layer order equal to the recorded order" is undefined for PLAT's new semantics

The rule is attributed to FTG, but FTG locks generated details only "when a person is manually edited".

claim: The embedding bridge copies FTG's `stateId` protocol without the store that makes it converge
claim_full: The bridge copies FTG's `stateId` optimistic-concurrency protocol without the server that makes it converge: FTG's Foundry module "never holds settlement state" and every iframe re-syncs from FTG's store, but PLAT has "no server", no command to load a document, no event carrying edit-log deltas and no version handshake, so after a GM's regenerate the players keep the old town, and clients keeping different replayable versions build different towns from one log; FTG also persists the current day and hour, favourites, notes and live public pins, for which PLAT has no state outside the model hash. The "sync service" deferral covers a hosted service, not the bridge's own contract (O11).
required_change: Make the host the store: LOAD_DOCUMENT {doc or url}, APPLY_EVENTS {baseStateId, events} (rebase or reject), DOCUMENT_CHANGED {stateId, events}, stateId = hash(document id, log length, last event hash); a version handshake (run the document's generatorVersion or open the snapshot read-only); a view-state section outside the model hash (current simulation time, favourites, notes, pins, player location, layer choice) with its own last-writer-wins rule; read-only viewers never write model events; test: host plus three headless clients applying interleaved events converge to one hash.
evidence: ARCH §11 bridge, §1.7 persistence, §2.9 Document, §6.4 ("last N minor generator versions replayable"), Deferrals; ftg-payload-visual §7.1–§7.2, §3.1 (field 22); ftg-posts-b T-31, T-32; ftg-posts-a §2.22 ("keeps the settlement in sync between players"); coverage audit N05 (COVERED). claim: The roster is a capped fixed-point iteration, not FTG's sequential loop, so it need not be prefix-stable in population
claim_full: The roster is a capped fixed-point iteration (≤ 6 iterations on integer counts with caps, size gates and shop-versus-core draws), which need not be prefix-stable in population: at 21 000 people it can hold fewer chandlers than at 20 000, so grow()'s "delta demand" goes negative and an epoch demolishes a survivor for no circumstantial reason, and §7.8's monotonicity sweep fails for the population control. FTG's loop is sequential (a virtual-population counter adds one building at a time until the target), so its manifest at P + ΔP extends the manifest at P.
required_change: Specify the roster as a sequential, prefix-stable process: a virtual-population counter in fixed steps, each step adding the next building by the ratio rules, every draw keyed by the building's ordinal; property test manifest(P2) ⊇ manifest(P1) for P2 > P1 on 1 000 seeds; epoch delta demand = the suffix; negative deltas only from declared circumstance events.
evidence: ARCH §10.2, §4.11 (grow(); coherence rule), §7.8, D-25, §16 M4 exit ("0 re-rolled survivors"); ftg-docs-params §3.3 (`createSettlement__dependency_graph.md` L25–43, verified by _critic-ftg §3 #32); owner EVOLUTION ruling.

claim: The growth heading model is under-specified; its curvature-continuous reading curls 600 m streets through 73–108°
claim_full: The growth heading model is under-specified: "a Gaussian on the rate of turn" with "curvature continuity" and headingSigma 2–9° reads as a random walk on curvature, under which a 600 m street (20 × 30 m) turns a median 73° at σ = 2° and 108° at σ = 3° (41 % / 58 % beyond 90°), so streets curl back and legality ends stages early; independent turns (6–9°) give no curvature continuity.
required_change: Specify a mean-reverting curvature process (Ornstein–Uhlenbeck on curvature with a stated correlation length, plus reversion toward the proposal's goal heading), headingSigma in degrees per 100 m, and a drift-distribution test.
